extraction.body: Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year. The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials. A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access. More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry. The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA. Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out. This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors. The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest. TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff . It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch after publication: “DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively. We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected. We will update the public when more information is available.” When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said. While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE. The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work. Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software. The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit. A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023. Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media. A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment. One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status . sources.title: OPM hack: China blamed for massive breach of US government data - The Guardian
passages: The Obama administration is scrambling to assess the impact of a massive data breach involving the agency that handles security clearances and US government employee records, with suspicion quickly falling on China, which has been accused of carrying out cyber-espionage against the US in the past.

Government officials familiar with the situation told the Associated Press the hack occurred at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and the Interior Department, and could potentially affect four million people at every federal agency.
China has routinely denied accusations by US investigators that hackers backed by the Chinese government have been behind attacks on US companies and federal agencies.
Obama has moved cybersecurity toward the top of his 2015 agenda after recent breaches and the White House says he raises the issue in meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
US military officials have become increasingly vocal about cyber espionage and attacks launched by China, Russia and others.
Senator Susan Collins, a Maine Republican, said the hackers were believed to be based in China.
Embassy spokesman Zhu Haiquan said China had made great efforts to combat cyberattacks and that tracking such events conducted across borders was difficult.
Ammon said sophisticated hacking operations funded by nation states were targeting system administrators and gaining access to massive amounts of data.
Reports in the New York Times and Washington Post on Thursday, both citing unnamed sources in the federal government, reported Chinese hackers were behind the breach.

In unveiling an updated cyber strategy in May, the US defense secretary, Ash Carter, singled out threats from Russia, China, Iran and North Korea and stressed the military’s ability to retaliate with cyber weapons.
In November a former DHS contractor disclosed another cyber-breach that compromised the private files of more than 25,000 DHS workers and thousands of other federal employees.

extraction.body: Denials from Beijing after computer systems are targeted at Office of Personnel Management, which holds details on entire staff of US government Denials from Beijing after computer systems are targeted at Office of Personnel Management, which holds details on entire staff of US government The Obama administration is scrambling to assess the impact of a massive data breach involving the agency that handles security clearances and US government employee records, with suspicion quickly falling on China, which has been accused of carrying out cyber-espionage against the US in the past. Government officials familiar with the situation told the Associated Press the hack occurred at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and the Interior Department, and could potentially affect four million people at every federal agency. The OPM is the human resources department for the federal government and does checks for security clearances. A US law enforcement source told the Reuters news agency on Thursday night that a “foreign entity or government” was believed to be behind the attack. Authorities were looking into a possible Chinese connection, the news agency said, quoting a source close to the matter. Chinese officials issued swift denials, with foreign ministry spokesman Hong Lei branding the accusations irresponsible and unscientific at a news briefing on Friday. “We know that hacker attacks are conducted anonymously, across nations, and that it is hard to track the source,” Hong said. “It’s irresponsible and unscientific to make conjectural, trumped-up allegations without deep investigation.” “The FBI is conducting an investigation to identify how and why this occurred,” the department of homeland security said in a statement on Thursday. “DHS is continuing to monitor federal networks for any suspicious activity and is working aggressively with the affected agencies to conduct investigative analysis to assess the extent of this alleged intrusion.” Reports in the New York Times and Washington Post on Thursday, both citing unnamed sources in the federal government, reported Chinese hackers were behind the breach. Senator Susan Collins, a Maine Republican, said the hackers were believed to be based in China. Collins, a member of the Senate intelligence committee, said the breach was “yet another indication of a foreign power probing successfully and focusing on what appears to be data that would identify people with security clearances”. The Chinese embassy in Washington responded that jumping to conclusions was “not responsible” and “counterproductive”. Embassy spokesman Zhu Haiquan said China had made great efforts to combat cyberattacks and that tracking such events conducted across borders was difficult. A Pentagon report in April said hackers associated with the Chinese government repeatedly targeted US military networks seeking intelligence during 2014. US Representative Adam Schiff, the ranking Democrat on the House select intelligence committee, said: “The last few months have seen a series of massive data breaches that have affected millions of Americans. He called the latest intrusion “among the most shocking because Americans may expect that federal computer networks are maintained with state-of-the-art defences”. “It’s clear that a substantial improvement in our cyber databases and defences is perilously overdue,” Schiff said. Senate intelligence committee chairman Richard Burr said the government must overhaul its cybersecurity defenses. “Our response to these attacks can no longer simply be notifying people after their personal information has been stolen,” he said. “We must start to prevent these breaches in the first place.” The largest federal employee union, the AFGE, said it would “demand accountability”. The union’s president, J David Cox, said it was working with the administration to ensure measures were taken to secure the personal information of affected employees. In November a former DHS contractor disclosed another cyber-breach that compromised the private files of more than 25,000 DHS workers and thousands of other federal employees. DHS said its intrusion detection system, known as Einstein, which screens federal internet traffic to identify potential cyber threats, identified the hack of OPM’s systems and the Interior Department’s data centre, which is shared by other federal agencies. “DHS is continuing to monitor federal networks for any suspicious activity and is working aggressively with the affected agencies to conduct investigative analysis to assess the extent of this alleged intrusion,” the statement said. The hack follows an attack on the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) that compromised the details of 100,000 taxpayers. On Wednesday the IRS commissioner John Koskinen appeared before a Senate committee and blamed the attack on underfunding and the agency’s inability to keep up with increasingly sophisticated threats. “This incident provides a stark reminder that even security controls that may have been adequate in the past can be overcome by hackers, who are anonymous, persistent and have access to vast amounts of personal data and knowledge,” J Russell George, treasury inspector general for tax administration, told the Senate finance committee. Ken Ammon, chief strategy officer at Xceedium, a government security contractor that specialises in securing privileged access to systems, said: “What we are seeing across the board is a particular weakness in our defence systems.” Ammon said sophisticated hacking operations funded by nation states were targeting system administrators and gaining access to massive amounts of data. “What you want to be able to do is cut your loses, make sure the attack is isolated to that particular individual and not the terabytes of information stored on the servers.” In April Barack Obama responded to a growing rash of attacks aimed at US computer networks by launching a sanctions program to target individuals and groups outside the United States that use cyber attacks to threaten US foreign policy, national security or economic stability. The move followed indictments of five Chinese military officers who were charged with economic espionage. US officials also pointed the finger directly at North Korea for a high-profile attack on Sony over a film spoof depicting the assassination of North Korea’s leader. China has routinely denied accusations by US investigators that hackers backed by the Chinese government have been behind attacks on US companies and federal agencies. Obama has moved cybersecurity toward the top of his 2015 agenda after recent breaches and the White House says he raises the issue in meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping. US military officials have become increasingly vocal about cyber espionage and attacks launched by China, Russia and others. In unveiling an updated cyber strategy in May, the US defense secretary, Ash Carter, singled out threats from Russia, China, Iran and North Korea and stressed the military’s ability to retaliate with cyber weapons.

passages: DHS officials have defended keeping agents’ identities secret by saying threats against the agency’s employees have multiplied since immigration enforcement intensified after Trump returned to the White House in 2025. ‘Massive’ impact The hackers accessed the dataset, which they dubbed “Icepick,” after obtaining an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS.
A group of hackers on Wednesday did what the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has steadfastly refused to do: expose the identities of thousands of federal immigration agents.

extraction.body: A group of hackers on Wednesday did what the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has steadfastly refused to do: expose the identities of thousands of federal immigration agents. The hackers breached a DHS internal database that lists the names, telephone numbers, email addresses and job assignments of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and other branches of the department. Many of the agents have been involved in highly contentious enforcement and deportation activities during the second Trump administration — including operations that led to the deaths of two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis and several other controversial shootings. DHS has refused to identify officers, even after they were involved in violent episodes, and agents routinely keep their names secret and wear face masks in public. Although some have been publicly outed through crowdsourcing, the release of the hacked data represents the broadest exposure of the government employees who have carried out President Donald Trump’s aggressive campaign against illegal immigration. Straight Arrow obtained the data from the Swiss hacker maia arson crimew, who is best known for locating an exposed copy of the U.S. government’s terrorism no-fly list, and the nonprofit leak archiver Distributed Denial of Secrets, known as DDoSecrets. A group calling itself the Department of Peace, or DoP, claimed responsibility for stealing the data from the DHS. Straight Arrow sought comment from DHS, ICE and CBP, but none immediately responded. DHS officials have defended keeping agents’ identities secret by saying threats against the agency’s employees have multiplied since immigration enforcement intensified after Trump returned to the White House in 2025. ‘Massive’ impact The hackers accessed the dataset, which they dubbed “Icepick,” after obtaining an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS. Okta, an identity and access management company based in San Francisco, allows federal employees to sign in once to access multiple work-approved apps without logging in to each one separately. ”This dataset is massive in terms of both size and impact,” crimew said in a statement. “It provides an unprecedented look into the Department of Homeland Security’s organizational structure, highlighting which people do what work across multiple DHS agencies, including ICE." The dataset contains information on almost 42,000 DHS employees, or about one-fifth of the agency’s workforce — including some who work in undercover operations. In addition to ICE and the border patrol, the exposed employees work for Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, the Federal Protective Service, the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers and the Science and Technology Directorate. ‘Architects and drivers’ of policy DDoSecrets opted to release the dataset to the public alongside a search tool developed by the hackers. The tool, according to the nonprofit, is intended to make searching “easier for reporters, activists, legal advocates and others interested in the dataset.” Journalist and DDoSecrets co-founder Emma Best described Icepick as much more than “an indiscriminate directory” of DHS employees. Instead, she said, the dataset identifies “many of the architects and drivers of DHS policy” as well as “officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations” and the “ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs.” An online search tool, known as icepi.cx, was built by crimew in an effort to further encourage and streamline investigations, including by the public. The tool allows users to search for DHS employees based on their names, agencies, job titles and locations. ”It is a complete game changer for anyone investigating DHS, simplifying the identification of agents and their lines of command,” said crimew, who was indicted but never convicted of hacking charges in the U.S. in 2021. “It provides FOIA material for years to come!” The data lists the names of user groups, to which DHS administrators can add individual employees based on their roles. The search tool highlights employees deemed high interest to the public, including those involved in well-publicized shootings. Using the online search tool, Straight Arrow located information on Jesus Ochoa and Raymundo Gutierrez, the two CBP agents who fatally shot protester Alex Pretti in Minneapolis in January. However, a search returned no results for Jonathan Ross, the agent who reportedly shot another protester, Renee Good, to death. ”By replacing the regime’s anonymity with accountability, Icepick and the tool developed by maia are catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests,” Best added. But a spokesperson for the hackers cited comments made by DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. ”On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was ’turning up the heat,’” the spokesperson said, referring to the secretary’s promise to intensify its crackdown following several controversial shootings. “This is what happens to ICE when you do that.”

extraction.body: The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon. Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels. The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release . The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick). Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois. On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch. Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end. By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College. coreStoryFacts.text: (Bloomberg) -- The Trump administration is offering as much as $5 billion in financing to Constellation Energy Corp. to upgrade and modernize the nuclear operator's fleet of reactors in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The Energy Department financing is part of President Donald Trump's push to expand nuclear power to meet growing electricity demand from data centers and support domestic manufacturing.
The funding follows an executive order that set a goal of adding 5 gigawatts of capacity through upgrades at existing nuclear plants, 96% of which has been achieved, the department said.
The financing, through the department's Office of Energy Dominance Financing, also includes an option to fund future uprates at other Constellation facilities.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright plans to announce the funding later Tuesday at an Illinois nuclear plant that will supply power to Alphabet Inc.'s Google.

extraction.body: The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon. Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels. The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release . The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick). Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois. On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch. Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon.

Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels.

sources.title: Apple's Redesigned MacBook Pro Has An OLED Touchscreen, Weighs Just Three Pounds - Engadget
passages: The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR, as it's officially called, is powered by either an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip, just like the non-touch models.
And as a nice throwback to older Apple laptops, its rear Apple logo also lights up.
As part of the new design, the OLED MacBook Pro features a Dynamic Island around its webcam, and Apple claims the 14-inch model weighs just three pounds.
That's a noticeable difference from the current MacBook Pro, which clocks in at 3.4 pounds.
Apple finally announced its long-rumored redesign today, and for the most part, it seems like the company went out of its way to create its most premium laptop yet.
It's clearly not meant for a regular consumer.
And thankfully, you've still got a useful array of ports: three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C connections, MagSafe, HDMI, headphone jack and an SDXC card slot.
So what's the point of a touchscreen MacBook Pro?
It makes the simple act of casually scrolling through articles and content easier, as we've seen on touchscreen-equipped Windows PC over the last 15 years.
But in the demo video above, we can also see people swiping on media and manipulating 3D objects.
It also looks like you can interact with iOS apps just as they would with a phone, which would be particularly useful to developers.
Third-party creator apps like Notion, Canva, Powerpoint and Blender will also work with the touchscreen natively.
The ProLED XDR screen reaches up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness, according to Apple, and it features an "industry-leading" 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
I can only imagine the eye-searing possibilities with this screen.
It also features a 120Hz refresh rate, just like existing MacBook Pros.
Thanks to the slimmer bezels, Apple was also able to squeeze in larger 14.2-inch and 16.3-inch screens.

There's no doubt Apple is late here, but there was also a certain wisdom in completely separating its touchscreen platforms (iOS, iPadOS and watchOS) from macOS, a platform that was designed entirely around traditional computer inputs.
With Windows 8, Microsoft rushed to enable PC touchscreens as a way to compete with the potential rise of iPads.
Apple didn't have the same pressure — especially since its glass touchpads offer an incredibly smooth scrolling experience on Macs.

It makes the simple act of casually scrolling through articles and content easier, as we've seen on touchscreen-equipped Windows PC over the last 15 years. But in the demo video above, we can also see people swiping on media and manipulating 3D objects. It also looks like you can interact with iOS apps just as they would with a phone, which would be particularly useful to developers. Apple says its own apps are optimized for the new MacBook Pro's touchscreen, and you'll be able to touch any app because macOS recognizes touch interactions as clicks. Third-party creator apps like Notion, Canva, Powerpoint and Blender will also work with the touchscreen natively.

There's no doubt Apple is late here, but there was also a certain wisdom in completely separating its touchscreen platforms (iOS, iPadOS and watchOS) from macOS, a platform that was designed entirely around traditional computer inputs. With Windows 8, Microsoft rushed to enable PC touchscreens as a way to compete with the potential rise of iPads. Apple didn't have the same pressure — especially since its glass touchpads offer an incredibly smooth scrolling experience on Macs.

MacBook Pros were always expensive, especially after Apple's recent hikes, but the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR pushes cost to a new extreme. A fully-decked out 16-inch model with an M5 Max chip, 128GB of RAM and 16TB of RAM costs an eye-watering $14,549. It's clearly not meant for a regular consumer. But given the rise in demand for powerful local AI hardware, I wouldn't be surprised if there's a robust market for an over-equipped MacBook Pro OLED.

sources.title: Amazon overhauls aging devices lineup with higher-priced Alexa tablet, dumping the budget Fire - CNBC
passages: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet.
But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show.
Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices .
Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video.
Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services.
It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021.
Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview.
"They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."

extraction.body: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy. The company unveiled 8-inch, 11-inch and 12-inch models, which start at $230 and run up to $550. All devices are available for preorder on Thursday and will begin shipping Oct. 14. Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services. It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins. The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021. Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant. The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199. The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices . Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch. And earlier this year, Apple raised its prices on MacBooks and iPads, while Nintendo hiked the price of its Switch 2 console. Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet. But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs." "I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview. "They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point." The company said the Alexa tablet's improved speed and performance, artificial intelligence features, and upgraded design warrant a higher price tag and put the devices on par with "the best tablets on the market." Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors. On the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the highest-end model, it incorporated "Nanomatte" display technology that was developed in partnership with Corning to "dramatically reduce screen glare." One of the most notable upgrades is that all of the devices run Google 's Android operating system, a major departure from earlier models, which relied on a custom Android version dubbed Fire OS and used Amazon's own app store, limiting the number of apps that were available. It's also the first time Amazon has attached a set of devices to the Alexa brand, the company's automated assistant first launched in 2014 via the Echo smart speaker. Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show. Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions. The company also introduced a new feature called "On-Screen Intelligence," where users can ask Alexa to look at what's on their screen and make suggestions or take actions. In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video. Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said. "She'll do the homework, and if things work out, she's going to bring up a shopping list where I can just hit buy now," Panay said. Amazon said it will continue to support the Fire lineup for four years after the final shipment and consumers can continue using their devices as they do today, but it is no longer manufacturing new units. "I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview. "They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."

The company said the Alexa tablet's improved speed and performance, artificial intelligence features, and upgraded design warrant a higher price tag and put the devices on par with "the best tablets on the market."

Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors. On the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the highest-end model, it incorporated "Nanomatte" display technology that was developed in partnership with Corning to "dramatically reduce screen glare."

One of the most notable upgrades is that all of the devices run Google 's Android operating system, a major departure from earlier models, which relied on a custom Android version dubbed Fire OS and used Amazon's own app store, limiting the number of apps that were available.

It's also the first time Amazon has attached a set of devices to the Alexa brand, the company's automated assistant first launched in 2014 via the Echo smart speaker. Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show. Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The company also introduced a new feature called "On-Screen Intelligence," where users can ask Alexa to look at what's on their screen and make suggestions or take actions.

In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video. Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.
"She'll do the homework, and if things work out, she's going to bring up a shopping list where I can just hit buy now," Panay said.

Amazon said it will continue to support the Fire lineup for four years after the final shipment and consumers can continue using their devices as they do today, but it is no longer manufacturing new units. The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.

sources.title: Amazon unveils new Echo devices, powered by its AI, Alexa+ - TechCrunch
passages: To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.
This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep.
The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon.
The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims.

As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs.
The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier.

Key to the devices are the Alexa+ integrations, allowing the speakers to respond to more queries than earlier models, offering support for natural language conversations, more complex questions, and soon, more add-ons and capabilities.

This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports. The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience. The new Echo devices launching today run on Amazon’s custom-designed silicon chips, the AZ3 and AZ3 Pro, which include an AI Accelerator designed to run AI edge models. The AZ3 enables better conversation detection on the Echo Dot, letting people talk to the device from anywhere in the room, while still filtering out background noise. The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims. The other three devices — the Studio, Show 8, and 11 — use the AZ3 Pro, which adds support for advanced language models and vision transformers. Plus, the AZ3 Pro-enabled devices include Ominisense, a custom sensor platform for ambient AI that uses the 13-megapixel camera on new Echo Show devices, audio, ultrasound, Wi-Fi radar, accelerometer, and Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI). With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night. The new Echo Dot Max, $99.99, adds nearly three times the bass for better sound. The two-way speaker includes a woofer for the deep bass and a custom tweeter for the high notes. The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon. The Echo Studio also includes a high-excursion woofer, spatial audio, and Dolby Atmos, and an upgraded light ring for better visual understanding of what Alexa is doing or processing. The company notes consumers can connect up to five Echo Studio or Echo Dot Max devices with compatible Fire TV sticks for an immersive sound system in their home, and it plans to sell products in Alexa Home Theater bundles. The AI assistant will run a new smart home experience called Alexa+ Home, which combines things like event summaries from Ring camera feeds and a smart home hub that supports Matter, Thread, and Zigbee. As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs. The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier. Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices. This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep. Other devices from Withings and Wyze will be supported in the future. sources.title: Amazon unveils its newest lineup of Alexa+ devices - About Amazon Australia
passages: Today, Amazon announced the latest generation of Alexa devices , each designed for Alexa+ and purpose-built for the moments and tasks customers turn to Alexa for most.
The next-generation Echo Dot is designed for everywhere you can imagine and packs even more into its compact form factor.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to hundreds of compatible devices such as lights, locks, thermostats right out of the box, plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 93 square metres of coverage to your existing network.
At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator built for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise.
Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.
Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon's best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful.
The camera enables a new Adaptive Volume feature that optimises playback as you move throughout the room.

What's new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time —explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you're away.
Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience.
There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely.

coreStoryFacts.text: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet.
But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show.
Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices .
Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video.
Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services.
It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021.
Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview.
"They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."
To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.

At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator built for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise.
Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.
Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon's best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful.
The camera enables a new Adaptive Volume feature that optimises playback as you move throughout the room.

What's new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time —explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you're away.
Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience.
There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely.

sources.title: Amazon overhauls aging devices lineup with higher-priced Alexa tablet, dumping the budget Fire - CNBC
passages: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet.
But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show.
Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices .
Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video.
Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services.
It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021.
Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview.
"They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."

Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch. And earlier this year, Apple raised its prices on MacBooks and iPads, while Nintendo hiked the price of its Switch 2 console. Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet. But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs." "I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview. "They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point." Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors. On the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the highest-end model, it incorporated "Nanomatte" display technology that was developed in partnership with Corning to "dramatically reduce screen glare." sources.title: Amazon unveils new Echo devices, powered by its AI, Alexa+ - TechCrunch
passages: To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.
This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep.
The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon.
The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims.

As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs.
The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier.

Key to the devices are the Alexa+ integrations, allowing the speakers to respond to more queries than earlier models, offering support for natural language conversations, more complex questions, and soon, more add-ons and capabilities.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to hundreds of compatible devices such as lights, locks, thermostats right out of the box, plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 93 square metres of coverage to your existing network. At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator built for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise. Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor. Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon's best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful. The camera enables a new Adaptive Volume feature that optimises playback as you move throughout the room. What's new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time —explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you're away. Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience. There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely.

The strategic emphasis on large-format displays aligns with consumer trends favoring hybrid media and control centers, with Amazon noting that its Echo Show family has emerged as its fastest-growing hardware tier, expanding at an annual rate exceeding 25%.

The comprehensive device refresh serves as an operational ramp for the company's generative voice agent, Alexa+, positioning specialized silicon and multi-sensor fusion hardware throughout the household.
By locking households deeper into its retail and entertainment channels, Amazon appears focused on reinforcing its competitive moat against encroaching smart home initiatives from Apple and Alphabet.

Beyond screen-based interaction, Amazon broadened its ambient hardware footprint with specialized room endpoints, including the $199.99 camera-free Echo Time smart alarm clock and a dedicated Alexa Photo Frame starting at $199.99.
These additions illustrate a segmentation strategy aimed at capturing sensitive personal spaces, such as bedrooms, where consumer privacy concerns previously limited smart device adoption.

sources.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices
passages: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock.
Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display.
Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame.
It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer.
It can also function like a digital photo frame.
The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen.

“Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.”
Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts.
Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos.
Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices.

“Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

“It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring.
It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release.
You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them.
Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera.
This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features.

extraction.body: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock. The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll. Aura is responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen. Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like a matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall. Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos. “It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them. The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale now , and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood. Meanwhile, the Echo Time clock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that people don’t want to rely on their phones for alarms, setting morning reminders, or checking the weather. “Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.” Amazon says that the Echo Time , which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for a Kids version, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up within a 10 to 60 minute window of your alarm time, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day. Like the popular Hatch alarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake. Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera. The biggest upgrade to the Echo Dot is that it now includes a built-in smart home hub, which also includes an eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage, helping it connect to lights, locks, and thermostats around your home. The new Echo Dot is also powered by Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon chip, which is said to make it better at on-device processing to speed up conversations with its AI, Alexa+. Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera. This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features. “Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.” The Echo Dot is available at $99.99, and the Echo Studio with Home Camera costs $249.99. Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display. Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame. It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer. It can also function like a digital photo frame. The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder for $499.99. The comprehensive device refresh serves as an operational ramp for the company's generative voice agent, Alexa+, positioning specialized silicon and multi-sensor fusion hardware throughout the household.

sources.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices
passages: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock.
Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display.
Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame.
It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer.
It can also function like a digital photo frame.
The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen.

“Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.”
Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts.
Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos.
Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices.

“Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

“It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring.
It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release.
You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them.
Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera.
This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features.

extraction.body: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock. The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll. Aura is responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen. Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like a matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall. Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos. “It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them. The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale now , and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood. Meanwhile, the Echo Time clock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that people don’t want to rely on their phones for alarms, setting morning reminders, or checking the weather. “Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa — checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does — so we designed an Echo specifically for it.” Amazon says that the Echo Time , which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for a Kids version, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up within a 10 to 60 minute window of your alarm time, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day. Like the popular Hatch alarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake. Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera. The biggest upgrade to the Echo Dot is that it now includes a built-in smart home hub, which also includes an eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage, helping it connect to lights, locks, and thermostats around your home. The new Echo Dot is also powered by Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon chip, which is said to make it better at on-device processing to speed up conversations with its AI, Alexa+. Amazon says its most advanced speaker, however, is the Echo Studio with Home Camera. This speaker doubles as a camera so you can check on your home while you’re out, and also has visual intelligence features. “Alexa can also see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help you in real time,” Amazon explained. “Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa+ to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.” The Echo Dot is available at $99.99, and the Echo Studio with Home Camera costs $249.99. Finally, Amazon unveiled the new Echo Show 16, which includes a 16-inch display. Amazon says the device has a 10% larger viewing area than its predecessor, but with a 40% smaller frame. It has Fire TV built in, plus Smart Home tools like Family Organizer. It can also function like a digital photo frame. The Echo Show 16 is available for preorder for $499.99. sources.title: Apple readies touch-screen MacBook Pro for 2026, reversing decade-long anti-touch stance
passages: Bloomberg News first reported in January 2023 that Apple was working on a touch-screen MacBook Pro.
For the revamped MacBook Pro, Apple is retiring the “notch” — the cutout at the top of the screen that houses the camera.
The current MacBook Pro design dates back to 2021, though Apple refreshed the 14-inch base version with an M5 chip on Wednesday.
The late Jobs, then Apple’s chief executive officer, said in 2010 that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical,” suggesting that they wouldn’t make sense for a computer screen.
As of now, Apple isn’t actively developing additional touch-screen Macs.
There have been concerns within Apple that touch-screen computers would cannibalize sales of iPads.
While the $999 MacBook Air remains the company’s bestselling laptop, a high-end touch-enabled MacBook Pro might entice customers to trade up — or switch from a Windows PC.
Apple’s iPad Magic Keyboard, introduced in 2020, also showed that customers were interested in combining a touch display with a traditional keyboard and trackpad.
Apple is exploring another major Mac change as well: a shift from the Touch ID fingerprint scanner to Face ID.
Apple shares pared their losses Thursday after Bloomberg reported on the plans.
The company is planning M5 Pro and M5 Max iterations for early 2026 that retain the current look, Bloomberg News has reported.
The company has also developed a reinforced hinge and screen hardware to prevent the display from bouncing back or moving when touched, a common drawback of existing touch PCs.
This follows a typical strategy for Apple, which offers new features on its top-end devices before bringing them down-market.
But tablet growth has already slowed in recent years, and touch screens have increasingly become must-have features for PCs.

extraction.body: Apple Inc. is preparing to finally launch a touch-screen version of its Mac computer, reversing course on a stance that dates back to co-founder Steve Jobs. The company is readying a revamped MacBook Pro with a touch display for late 2026 or early 2027, according to people with knowledge of the matter. In making the move, Apple is following the rest of the computing industry, which embraced touch-screen laptops more than a decade ago. The company has taken years to formulate its approach to the market, aiming to improve on current designs. Bloomberg News first reported in January 2023 that Apple was working on a touch-screen MacBook Pro. The new laptops will feature displays with OLED technology — short for organic light-emitting diode — the same standard used in iPhones and iPad Pros, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the products haven’t been announced. A spokesperson for Cupertino, Calif.a-based Apple declined to comment. Apple shares pared their losses Thursday after Bloomberg reported on the plans. The touch-screen MacBook Pro will retain a full trackpad and keyboard — mirroring the approach of PC makers like Dell Technologies Inc., Acer Inc., Lenovo Group Ltd. and Microsoft Corp. That means users won’t have to rely on the touch display if they don’t want to. For the revamped MacBook Pro, Apple is retiring the “notch” — the cutout at the top of the screen that houses the camera. In its place, the company will adopt a so-called hole-punch design that leaves a display area around the sensor. The company has also developed a reinforced hinge and screen hardware to prevent the display from bouncing back or moving when touched, a common drawback of existing touch PCs. Because of the pricier components, the new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are likely to cost a few hundred dollars more than current versions. Today’s non-touch models with high-end chips start at $1,999 for the 14-inch version and $2,499 for the larger one. The current MacBook Pro design dates back to 2021, though Apple refreshed the 14-inch base version with an M5 chip on Wednesday. The company is planning M5 Pro and M5 Max iterations for early 2026 that retain the current look, Bloomberg News has reported. As of now, Apple isn’t actively developing additional touch-screen Macs. Instead, it’s waiting to see the market’s reaction to the touch version of the MacBook Pro, the people said. This follows a typical strategy for Apple, which offers new features on its top-end devices before bringing them down-market. For years, Apple resisted the idea of touch-screen Macs, arguing that PCs with the feature were difficult to use and not ergonomic. It instead pushed users who want touch interfaces to buy iPads. The late Jobs, then Apple’s chief executive officer, said in 2010 that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical,” suggesting that they wouldn’t make sense for a computer screen. Apple tried a compromise in 2016 with the Touch Bar, a touch-screen strip that sat above the keyboard. There have been concerns within Apple that touch-screen computers would cannibalize sales of iPads. But tablet growth has already slowed in recent years, and touch screens have increasingly become must-have features for PCs. And Apple has bridged the gap between iPads and Macs in other ways: The devices now have unified interfaces, processors and app ecosystems. Apple’s iPad Magic Keyboard, introduced in 2020, also showed that customers were interested in combining a touch display with a traditional keyboard and trackpad. The accessory has become central to the iPad Pro’s sales pitch, letting users easily shift between touch and traditional controls. Adding a touch screen to the MacBook Pro could push users upmarket, creating new revenue opportunities for Apple. While the $999 MacBook Air remains the company’s bestselling laptop, a high-end touch-enabled MacBook Pro might entice customers to trade up — or switch from a Windows PC. Other new Macs in development include updated MacBook Airs with the M5 chip. The company is also working on a refreshed Mac Studio, Mac mini, and a pair of external Mac monitors dubbed J427 and J527. Apple is exploring another major Mac change as well: a shift from the Touch ID fingerprint scanner to Face ID.
