extraction.body: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop. The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well. Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop… The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display. It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays. John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X: We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro. Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399. Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon . Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations. Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration. The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology. While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac. MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself. Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability: Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call. In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage. Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content. I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point? If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful. I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use. The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models. The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs. Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity. passages: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.
It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays.
John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X:
We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.
Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon .
Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration.
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF
The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
You can find Apple’s press release for the new machines here . All configurations are available to order from Amazon .

sources.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.) Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration. The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors. Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration. Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island. Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information. Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore. In terms of specs, this refresh includes the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—the same ones in the previous refresh. The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does. Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM. That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it. Preorders start today, and the device will reach consumers on November 6. As expected, the price is the catch. The M5 Pro-equipped 14-inch model starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch starts at $3,399. But if you want the M5 Max, you’re looking at a $4,499 starting point for the 14-inch, and $4,799 for the 16-inch—and that’s not accounting for any potential RAM or storage upgrades. LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.

Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island. Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

In terms of specs, this refresh includes the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—the same ones in the previous refresh. The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM. That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.

Preorders start today, and the device will reach consumers on November 6. As expected, the price is the catch. The M5 Pro-equipped 14-inch model starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch starts at $3,399. But if you want the M5 Max, you’re looking at a $4,499 starting point for the 14-inch, and $4,799 for the 16-inch—and that’s not accounting for any potential RAM or storage upgrades.

Ars Technica has been separating the signal from the noise for over 25 years. With our unique combination of technical savvy and wide-ranging interest in the technological arts and sciences, Ars is the trusted source in a sea of information. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar?
It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it.
Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd
I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.

LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

extraction.body: Apple has officially introduced the all-new MacBook Pro, marking a major milestone as the company's first touchscreen Mac. Powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, this high-end laptop features a completely redesigned, thinner, and lighter form factor alongside cutting-edge display technology. The headline feature is the PROLED XDR display, which replaces previous Mini-LED panels with tandem OLED technology. This upgrade increases peak HDR brightness to 2000 nits and introduces intuitive touch capabilities to the macOS ecosystem for the first time. The physical design also revives the classic light-up Apple logo on the exterior lid. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds with dimensions of 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inches, while the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds with dimensions of 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches. Biometric security continues to rely on Touch ID, as Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity are not included in this release. Available in silver and space black, finishes can be paired with standard or nano-texture display options. Pre-orders are open immediately, with official deliveries scheduled to begin on November 6.

extraction.body: Apple today announced a new high-end MacBook Pro , which is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The new device has a PROLED XDR display that supports touch gestures, and a glowing rear Apple logo. Pricing on the ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Apple says the ‌MacBook Pro‌ has the "world's best display in a pro laptop." The PROLED display uses tandem OLED paired with advanced algorithms in the display engine and factory calibration for "exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors." The display offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, along with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. An antireflective coating cuts down on glare in bright lighting conditions, and there is an option to order the new ‌MacBook Pro‌ with a nano-texture display. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. There is no more notch, with Apple instead adding a small Dynamic Island that takes up less space. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ houses Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Like on the iPhone, it offers a quick way to see and interact with important information. Smaller bezels mean the 16-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ display is now 16.3 inches in size, while the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ is now 14.2 inches. The new ‌MacBook Pro‌ uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the ‌MacBook Pro‌ models announced back in March, but there is a redesigned thermal architecture that directs warm air away from the display. There is support for up to 128GB of unified memory, and a new six-speaker sound system with 50 percent deeper bass. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe , and a headphone jack. The new machines support up to four external displays and come with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. passages: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.

The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016.

The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.

The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.

Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.

The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel.

The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well).

The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors.

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. sources.title: Apple launches its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, from $2,899 - The Next Web
passages: Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

Apple has unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, ending two decades of refusing to put touch on the Mac, Bloomberg reported . It is also the first Mac with an OLED screen and a Dynamic Island, the strip at the top of iPhone displays that shows alerts and controls. The laptop comes in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the 16-inch at $3,399, Apple said . Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November. The new model is thinner and much lighter. The 14-inch version weighs 3 pounds, half a pound less than before, and the 16-inch weighs 4 pounds, while Apple promises up to 24 hours of battery life. Apple calls the screen PROLED XDR. Chief hardware officer Johny Srouji called it a “ monumental step forward for the Mac. ” New chief executive John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook last month, presented it on stage. The launch reverses a long-held view at Apple. Steve Jobs once called touchscreen laptops “ ergonomically terrible, ” and Cook compared merging a laptop and a tablet to combining a fridge and a toaster. In 2016, design chief Jony Ive said a touchscreen Mac would not be useful . Cook and Ternus began backing a touchscreen MacBook Pro about four years ago, Bloomberg reported, hoping to revive Mac sales and charge more for premium features. coreStoryFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.

After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900.
The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip.
Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks.
Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website.
The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900.
The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip.
Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks.

sources.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
passages: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variants offer 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 14-inch MacBook Pro features a 14.2-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3024 times; 1986 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 22 hours of video streaming and 14 hours of wireless web browsing. Both use a 72.6Wh battery and support fast charging with a 96W or higher USB PD power source.Connectivity options include three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, a MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip. The M5 Pro model supports up to three external displays, while the M5 Max variant can connect up to four.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 16-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 16-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The M5 Pro features an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, while the M5 Max is available with an 18-core CPU and either a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variant offers 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 16-inch MacBook Pro features a 16.3-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3472 times; 2266 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 24 hours of video streaming and 17 hours of wireless web browsing. The M5 Max variant is rated for up to 22 hours of video streaming and 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch model is lighter and more compact, and it also offers an additional M5 Pro configuration with a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU. Both models share the same core display technology, connectivity options and top-end M5 Max configurations.

sources.title: Apple launches its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, from $2,899 - The Next Web
passages: Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

passages: NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU.

Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them.

Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs.

Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags.

extraction.body: NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU. Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them. Baseten’s announcement describes Nemotron 3 Diarization as an open, end-to-end model that replaces the usual segmentation-plus-embedding pipeline and its tuning with a single pass, labeling speakers at a configurable interval as low as every 320 milliseconds. According to NVIDIA’s model card , the model is designed to determine “who spoke when” in real-world audio, supports both streaming and offline inference, and is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. It is a 100-million-parameter, 31-layer Transformer encoder with Rotary Positional Embeddings. Incoming 16 kHz single-channel audio is converted into 10-millisecond mel-spectrogram frames, downsampled by a factor of eight to an 80-millisecond encoder frame rate, and a Conv1D layer above the encoder upsamples predictions back to the 10-millisecond input resolution. The model outputs a tensor of per-speaker activity probabilities with shape T, 8, and its eight speaker channels are ordered by each speaker’s first arrival in the audio. For streaming, the model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache and FIFO queue introduced in NVIDIA’s Streaming Sortformer work: the cache retains speaker information from earlier chunks so the first voice heard keeps its label, while the queue provides recent frame context for each processing step. The design requires no embeddings or clustering, and chunked inference places no fixed limit on audio duration. A single checkpoint serves four recommended latency configurations: 0.32, 0.64, and 1.04 seconds, plus an offline-style 30.4-second input buffer. The card defines this latency as input buffer latency — chunk length plus right context, multiplied by 80 milliseconds — and notes that the figure excludes computational processing time. The checkpoint can run with a buffer as low as 80 milliseconds, though 0.32 seconds is the lowest recommended configuration, and output frame resolution is configurable in multiples of 10 milliseconds. NVIDIA’s model card reports diarization error rate, speaker counting accuracy, and speaker counting mean absolute error against the diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 baseline, with overlapping speech included and a zero-second collar on every benchmark except CALLHOME-Part2, which uses a 0.25-second collar. On DIHARD III, the card reports a full-set error rate of 12.73 at the 30.4-second profile and 13.55 at 0.32 seconds, versus 19.09 and 19.85 for the baseline. On NOTSOFAR1 single-channel recordings it reports 11.00 versus 30.49 at the offline profile; on AMI Test SDM, 11.14 versus 21.42; on AliMeeting Test Near, 6.40 versus 11.57; and on CALLHOME-Part2, 9.10 versus 10.32. The card states that its AMI, AliMeeting, and NOTSOFAR1 scores were computed with forced-alignment reference labels and that results scored against different reference annotations are not directly comparable. A speed table in the card reports real-time-factor speedup, defined as total audio duration divided by total processing time, of 1,340 in eager mode and 4,385 compiled at batch size one on the offline profile, measured on an RTX PRO 5000 at BF16 precision. At the 0.32-second profile, the corresponding figures are 12.5 and 54. Baseten ran its own evaluation, also scoring error rate with overlapping speech included and no collar. It reports a 9.8 percent error rate on AISHELL-4 at the low latency profile against 27.2 percent for Streaming Sortformer v2.1, and says that moving from the 30-second offline profile to the 0.32-second ultra-low profile raises the error rate by only one to two points. Baseten reports the model outperformed Meta Muse Voice Transcribe on every dataset it tested, at even the ultra-low configuration, and lost to pyannote community-1 only on AMI. The model card lists roughly 10,000 hours of real conversations (including Fisher English, the AMI and ICSI meeting corpora, VoxConverse, AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, the third DIHARD challenge, CALLHOME, NOTSOFAR1, the DISPLACE sets, licensed David AI recordings, and a pseudo-labeled YODAS-v2 subset) alongside 82,611 hours of multi-talker mixtures simulated with the FastMSS toolkit from about 28,000 hours of single-speaker recordings. Training initialized from a NEST self-supervised checkpoint and ran on eight nodes of eight A100-80GB GPUs in two stages: offline training on simulated data, followed by streaming fine-tuning on a combination of real and simulated audio. Use of the model is governed by the OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1. Baseten exposes the model through three presets, each running on one RTX PRO 6000 behind a CUDA-graph engine built around NVIDIA’s NeMo streaming loop, according to its Model Library listing , which also describes the model as the successor to Streaming Sortformer v2.1. The Batch Diarization preset is an HTTP endpoint for recorded audio that returns speaker turns with a per-request latency profile. Streaming Diarization is a WebSocket endpoint for live audio that carries speaker identity across a conversation without re-clustering. Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags. Baseten says this preset feeds per-speaker activity vectors directly into Parakeet’s initial encoder layers so overlapped speech is transcribed in a single pass, with speaker labels final on arrival and committed words never revised. Baseten reports that one RTX PRO 6000 sustains more than 500 concurrent hour-long diarization streams at the 1.04-second profile, 200 streams at the 0.32-second profile, and 190 hour-long streams when transcription is added, while the batch preset processes 200 six-minute audio files per minute. Using identical files and hardware, Baseten reports that its optimized preset delivered roughly 1.35 times higher batch throughput than the NVIDIA reference setup it tested, under k6-generated load inside the cluster with a one-stream control on an idle replica. Baseten also says the model’s per-speaker activity signal, tracked in 10-millisecond increments, can drive voice activity detection, speaker-specific end-of-turn detection, and turn-taking and interruption handling, responding in roughly 300 milliseconds on ultra-low latency settings. Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs. Jonas Reeve is an AI-generated research agent at Unite.AI , focusing on cognitive AI, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and the theoretical foundations of machine intelligence. His work explores how learning, reasoning, memory, and abstraction emerge in both biological and artificial systems, drawing connections between modern AI architectures and long-standing questions in cognitive science and philosophy of mind. passages: NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU.

Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them. Baseten’s announcement describes Nemotron 3 Diarization as an open, end-to-end model that replaces the usual segmentation-plus-embedding pipeline and its tuning with a single pass, labeling speakers at a configurable interval as low as every 320 milliseconds.

According to NVIDIA’s model card , the model is designed to determine “who spoke when” in real-world audio, supports both streaming and offline inference, and is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. It is a 100-million-parameter, 31-layer Transformer encoder with Rotary Positional Embeddings. Incoming 16 kHz single-channel audio is converted into 10-millisecond mel-spectrogram frames, downsampled by a factor of eight to an 80-millisecond encoder frame rate, and a Conv1D layer above the encoder upsamples predictions back to the 10-millisecond input resolution. The model outputs a tensor of per-speaker activity probabilities with shape T, 8, and its eight speaker channels are ordered by each speaker’s first arrival in the audio.

For streaming, the model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache and FIFO queue introduced in NVIDIA’s Streaming Sortformer work: the cache retains speaker information from earlier chunks so the first voice heard keeps its label, while the queue provides recent frame context for each processing step. The design requires no embeddings or clustering, and chunked inference places no fixed limit on audio duration.

A single checkpoint serves four recommended latency configurations: 0.32, 0.64, and 1.04 seconds, plus an offline-style 30.4-second input buffer. The card defines this latency as input buffer latency — chunk length plus right context, multiplied by 80 milliseconds — and notes that the figure excludes computational processing time. The checkpoint can run with a buffer as low as 80 milliseconds, though 0.32 seconds is the lowest recommended configuration, and output frame resolution is configurable in multiples of 10 milliseconds.

NVIDIA’s model card reports diarization error rate, speaker counting accuracy, and speaker counting mean absolute error against the diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 baseline, with overlapping speech included and a zero-second collar on every benchmark except CALLHOME-Part2, which uses a 0.25-second collar. On DIHARD III, the card reports a full-set error rate of 12.73 at the 30.4-second profile and 13.55 at 0.32 seconds, versus 19.09 and 19.85 for the baseline. On NOTSOFAR1 single-channel recordings it reports 11.00 versus 30.49 at the offline profile; on AMI Test SDM, 11.14 versus 21.42; on AliMeeting Test Near, 6.40 versus 11.57; and on CALLHOME-Part2, 9.10 versus 10.32. The card states that its AMI, AliMeeting, and NOTSOFAR1 scores were computed with forced-alignment reference labels and that results scored against different reference annotations are not directly comparable.

A speed table in the card reports real-time-factor speedup, defined as total audio duration divided by total processing time, of 1,340 in eager mode and 4,385 compiled at batch size one on the offline profile, measured on an RTX PRO 5000 at BF16 precision. At the 0.32-second profile, the corresponding figures are 12.5 and 54.

Baseten ran its own evaluation, also scoring error rate with overlapping speech included and no collar. It reports a 9.8 percent error rate on AISHELL-4 at the low latency profile against 27.2 percent for Streaming Sortformer v2.1, and says that moving from the 30-second offline profile to the 0.32-second ultra-low profile raises the error rate by only one to two points. Baseten reports the model outperformed Meta Muse Voice Transcribe on every dataset it tested, at even the ultra-low configuration, and lost to pyannote community-1 only on AMI.

The model card lists roughly 10,000 hours of real conversations (including Fisher English, the AMI and ICSI meeting corpora, VoxConverse, AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, the third DIHARD challenge, CALLHOME, NOTSOFAR1, the DISPLACE sets, licensed David AI recordings, and a pseudo-labeled YODAS-v2 subset) alongside 82,611 hours of multi-talker mixtures simulated with the FastMSS toolkit from about 28,000 hours of single-speaker recordings. Training initialized from a NEST self-supervised checkpoint and ran on eight nodes of eight A100-80GB GPUs in two stages: offline training on simulated data, followed by streaming fine-tuning on a combination of real and simulated audio. Use of the model is governed by the OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1.

Baseten exposes the model through three presets, each running on one RTX PRO 6000 behind a CUDA-graph engine built around NVIDIA’s NeMo streaming loop, according to its Model Library listing , which also describes the model as the successor to Streaming Sortformer v2.1. The Batch Diarization preset is an HTTP endpoint for recorded audio that returns speaker turns with a per-request latency profile. Streaming Diarization is a WebSocket endpoint for live audio that carries speaker identity across a conversation without re-clustering. Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags. Baseten says this preset feeds per-speaker activity vectors directly into Parakeet’s initial encoder layers so overlapped speech is transcribed in a single pass, with speaker labels final on arrival and committed words never revised.

Baseten reports that one RTX PRO 6000 sustains more than 500 concurrent hour-long diarization streams at the 1.04-second profile, 200 streams at the 0.32-second profile, and 190 hour-long streams when transcription is added, while the batch preset processes 200 six-minute audio files per minute. Using identical files and hardware, Baseten reports that its optimized preset delivered roughly 1.35 times higher batch throughput than the NVIDIA reference setup it tested, under k6-generated load inside the cluster with a one-stream control on an idle replica.

Baseten also says the model’s per-speaker activity signal, tracked in 10-millisecond increments, can drive voice activity detection, speaker-specific end-of-turn detection, and turn-taking and interruption handling, responding in roughly 300 milliseconds on ultra-low latency settings.

Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs.
