It is an open speech model that handles transcription, speaker attribution, translation and audio question answering in one set of weights. Coverage from SiliconANGLE, TechCrunch, AI Insider and Technology Org put the launch at the top of today’s AI news. The pitch is simple. Instead of chaining a speech recognizer, a diarization tool, a translation engine and a text model, a developer points one model at an audio file and tells it what to do in plain language. The reports describe a single model that covers 40 languages for transcription, 31 languages for translation to or from English, and speaker attribution in 13 languages. This piece sorts what the announcement confirms from what it leaves open. It also places the release next to NVIDIA’s earlier Nemotron 3.5 open models and the wider fight over open-weight AI. The Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe name matters here, because the “all-in-one adaptable” wording floating around headlines is not confirmed as official NVIDIA language. Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. The official product name found in the reporting is NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe. NVIDIA describes it as an open speech LLM built for intelligent transcription. In practice that means an open-weight model that listens to audio and produces text, but also reasons about what it heard. The “speech LLM” label is the key. Classic automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems turn sound into words and stop there. A speech LLM accepts audio as input to a language model, which lets it follow instructions. Ask it for a verbatim transcript and it keeps the stumbles and filler words. Ask for written form and it cleans the text up. Ask a question about the recording and it answers. Every figure below comes from the verified launch details. Anything the sources do not state, such as accuracy scores, parameter counts or licensing terms, stays out of the table on purpose. Read the three language counts together. Forty languages for plain transcription is the widest net. Translation narrows to 31 languages, and every one of those pairs touches English. Speaker attribution narrows again to 13. The model does more in some languages than in others, and buyers should plan around that gradient. The headline capability is consolidation. NVIDIA says one model covers four jobs that teams usually split across separate tools. Those jobs are transcription, speaker attribution, translation and question answering over audio. Transcription style is a real product decision. A court reporter wants every false start preserved. A podcast editor wants a clean paragraph. Most speech systems force that choice at build time through separate models or post-processing rules. According to the reports, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe makes it a runtime instruction, so the same weights serve both audiences. Speaker attribution answers the question of who said what. The model identifies up to eight speakers in a recording and supports this in 13 languages. Word timestamps tie each word to a position in the audio, which makes it possible to jump from a transcript line straight to the sound, build subtitles, or search a long meeting. What a unified model does offer with certainty is fewer moving parts. One deployment, one set of weights to version, one failure surface to monitor. For small teams that alone can decide the build-versus-buy math. The language numbers deserve a slower read than the headline gives them. A claim of 40 languages tells you the model can transcribe in 40. It does not tell you the quality is equal across all of them, and the sources publish no per-language accuracy figures. Translation is anchored on English. The 31 languages are described as to or from English, so a Spanish-to-Japanese request would not be a listed direction. Teams that need direct pairs would have to route through English, which can compound errors, or test the model themselves. Speaker attribution is the narrowest at 13 languages. If your audio is Hindi, Swahili or Vietnamese, check the model card before you promise speaker labels to a customer. Transcription may work while attribution does not. Voice products in fast-growing markets feel this gap most. Our earlier look at India’s voice AI latency budget shows how tight real-time speech constraints get once multilingual audio enters the picture. The reports say the model handles recordings up to one hour and identifies up to eight speakers. Those are practical limits, and they map neatly onto real workloads. A board meeting, a lecture, a podcast episode or a customer call all fit inside an hour. A full-day deposition or a conference keynote with a long Q&A does not. A model with a stated one-hour cap at least tells you where to look. The sources list no price for Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe. coreStoryFacts.text: SAN FRANCISCO, July 21, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Deepgram today announced an initiative to bring enterprise-grade speech recognition directly onto PCs powered by Snapdragon® processors.

By optimizing Deepgram's Nova-3 speech-to-text model on the Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU in the Snapdragon X Series platform, Deepgram is enabling developers and device manufacturers to deliver real-time voice experiences with greater speed, privacy, and reliability, without relying on a cloud connection.
This effort opens the door to further integration of voice into a new generation of intelligent applications across automotive, mobile, AI PC, XR, industrial edge, IoT, and wearable devices.
"We recognize that voice AI technologies serve different needs.

That's why we value our work with Deepgram – because accuracy, latency, reliability, and scalability matter for developers building automotive systems, healthcare applications, industrial solutions, and other mission-critical experiences," said Upendra Kulkarni, Vice President Product Management, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
Deepgram's voice-native foundation models, accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted/on-premises APIs, deliver unmatched accuracy, low latency, and competitive pricing.
Having processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed over 1 trillion words, there is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

"The future of voice-first interaction is about meeting users wherever they are — in a vehicle, on a factory floor, inside an XR headset — without compromising on accuracy or responsiveness," said Abe Pursell, Vice President, Business Development and Partnerships, Deepgram.

We're bringing Deepgram Nova-3 directly to the ecosystem of PCs with Snapdragon, providing a foundation to build voice into products that work wherever people happen to be, regardless of network conditions."
It is the first voice AI model to offer real-time multilingual transcription.
Qualcomm, Hexagon and Snapdragon are trademarks or registered trademarks of Qualcomm Incorporated.

Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops , to Blackwell datacenter chips.
It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters).
Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe , a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages.
It also released version 2 of Granary, its open source speech dataset.
These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace.
Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language.
One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not livestreams.

NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU.

Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them.

Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs.

NVIDIA’s model card reports diarization error rate, speaker counting accuracy, and speaker counting mean absolute error against the diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 baseline, with overlapping speech included and a zero-second collar on every benchmark except CALLHOME-Part2, which uses a 0.25-second collar.
The Batch Diarization preset is an HTTP endpoint for recorded audio that returns speaker turns with a per-request latency profile.

Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags.

NVIDIA has used it for a line of open models, and the 3.5 label ties this speech release to that family.
The sources do not describe how the speech model was trained or how it relates to its siblings, so that connection stays at the level of naming and timing.
Instead of chaining a speech recognizer, a diarization tool, a translation engine and a text model, a developer points one model at an audio file and tells it what to do in plain language.
Transcription style is a real product decision.
A court reporter wants every false start preserved.
Most speech systems force that choice at build time through separate models or post-processing rules.
That is consistent with an open-weight release distributed through Hugging Face and ModelScope, where the model files are the product.
The cited reports do not spell out the license, so check the model card for commercial-use terms before you build on it.
The language numbers deserve a slower read than the headline gives them.
A claim of 40 languages tells you the model can transcribe in 40.
It does not tell you the quality is equal across all of them, and the sources publish no per-language accuracy figures.
Reports list 40 languages for transcription, 31 languages for translation to or from English, and 13 languages for speaker attribution.
NVIDIA says one model covers four jobs that teams usually split across separate tools.
OpenAI open-sourced Whisper in 2022, and that release made open-weight transcription a baseline expectation.
NVIDIA packaged them into one open model and put it where developers already shop for weights.

extraction.body: NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU. Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them. Baseten’s announcement describes Nemotron 3 Diarization as an open, end-to-end model that replaces the usual segmentation-plus-embedding pipeline and its tuning with a single pass, labeling speakers at a configurable interval as low as every 320 milliseconds. According to NVIDIA’s model card , the model is designed to determine “who spoke when” in real-world audio, supports both streaming and offline inference, and is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. It is a 100-million-parameter, 31-layer Transformer encoder with Rotary Positional Embeddings. Incoming 16 kHz single-channel audio is converted into 10-millisecond mel-spectrogram frames, downsampled by a factor of eight to an 80-millisecond encoder frame rate, and a Conv1D layer above the encoder upsamples predictions back to the 10-millisecond input resolution. The model outputs a tensor of per-speaker activity probabilities with shape T, 8, and its eight speaker channels are ordered by each speaker’s first arrival in the audio. For streaming, the model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache and FIFO queue introduced in NVIDIA’s Streaming Sortformer work: the cache retains speaker information from earlier chunks so the first voice heard keeps its label, while the queue provides recent frame context for each processing step. The design requires no embeddings or clustering, and chunked inference places no fixed limit on audio duration. A single checkpoint serves four recommended latency configurations: 0.32, 0.64, and 1.04 seconds, plus an offline-style 30.4-second input buffer. The card defines this latency as input buffer latency — chunk length plus right context, multiplied by 80 milliseconds — and notes that the figure excludes computational processing time. The checkpoint can run with a buffer as low as 80 milliseconds, though 0.32 seconds is the lowest recommended configuration, and output frame resolution is configurable in multiples of 10 milliseconds. NVIDIA’s model card reports diarization error rate, speaker counting accuracy, and speaker counting mean absolute error against the diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 baseline, with overlapping speech included and a zero-second collar on every benchmark except CALLHOME-Part2, which uses a 0.25-second collar. On DIHARD III, the card reports a full-set error rate of 12.73 at the 30.4-second profile and 13.55 at 0.32 seconds, versus 19.09 and 19.85 for the baseline. On NOTSOFAR1 single-channel recordings it reports 11.00 versus 30.49 at the offline profile; on AMI Test SDM, 11.14 versus 21.42; on AliMeeting Test Near, 6.40 versus 11.57; and on CALLHOME-Part2, 9.10 versus 10.32. The card states that its AMI, AliMeeting, and NOTSOFAR1 scores were computed with forced-alignment reference labels and that results scored against different reference annotations are not directly comparable. A speed table in the card reports real-time-factor speedup, defined as total audio duration divided by total processing time, of 1,340 in eager mode and 4,385 compiled at batch size one on the offline profile, measured on an RTX PRO 5000 at BF16 precision. At the 0.32-second profile, the corresponding figures are 12.5 and 54. Baseten ran its own evaluation, also scoring error rate with overlapping speech included and no collar. It reports a 9.8 percent error rate on AISHELL-4 at the low latency profile against 27.2 percent for Streaming Sortformer v2.1, and says that moving from the 30-second offline profile to the 0.32-second ultra-low profile raises the error rate by only one to two points. Baseten reports the model outperformed Meta Muse Voice Transcribe on every dataset it tested, at even the ultra-low configuration, and lost to pyannote community-1 only on AMI. The model card lists roughly 10,000 hours of real conversations (including Fisher English, the AMI and ICSI meeting corpora, VoxConverse, AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, the third DIHARD challenge, CALLHOME, NOTSOFAR1, the DISPLACE sets, licensed David AI recordings, and a pseudo-labeled YODAS-v2 subset) alongside 82,611 hours of multi-talker mixtures simulated with the FastMSS toolkit from about 28,000 hours of single-speaker recordings. Training initialized from a NEST self-supervised checkpoint and ran on eight nodes of eight A100-80GB GPUs in two stages: offline training on simulated data, followed by streaming fine-tuning on a combination of real and simulated audio. Use of the model is governed by the OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1. Baseten exposes the model through three presets, each running on one RTX PRO 6000 behind a CUDA-graph engine built around NVIDIA’s NeMo streaming loop, according to its Model Library listing , which also describes the model as the successor to Streaming Sortformer v2.1. The Batch Diarization preset is an HTTP endpoint for recorded audio that returns speaker turns with a per-request latency profile. Streaming Diarization is a WebSocket endpoint for live audio that carries speaker identity across a conversation without re-clustering. Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags. Baseten says this preset feeds per-speaker activity vectors directly into Parakeet’s initial encoder layers so overlapped speech is transcribed in a single pass, with speaker labels final on arrival and committed words never revised. Baseten reports that one RTX PRO 6000 sustains more than 500 concurrent hour-long diarization streams at the 1.04-second profile, 200 streams at the 0.32-second profile, and 190 hour-long streams when transcription is added, while the batch preset processes 200 six-minute audio files per minute. Using identical files and hardware, Baseten reports that its optimized preset delivered roughly 1.35 times higher batch throughput than the NVIDIA reference setup it tested, under k6-generated load inside the cluster with a one-stream control on an idle replica. Baseten also says the model’s per-speaker activity signal, tracked in 10-millisecond increments, can drive voice activity detection, speaker-specific end-of-turn detection, and turn-taking and interruption handling, responding in roughly 300 milliseconds on ultra-low latency settings. Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs. passages: NVIDIA on September 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight speaker diarization model that identifies up to eight speakers in live or recorded audio, and Baseten announced same-day serving support with batch, streaming, and diarized-transcription presets that each run on one RTX PRO 6000 GPU.

Speaker diarization segments an audio stream by when each distinct speaker is talking, outputs timings for each voice, and assigns every span a consistent label; paired with transcription, it attributes transcribed words to the person who said them. Baseten’s announcement describes Nemotron 3 Diarization as an open, end-to-end model that replaces the usual segmentation-plus-embedding pipeline and its tuning with a single pass, labeling speakers at a configurable interval as low as every 320 milliseconds.

According to NVIDIA’s model card , the model is designed to determine “who spoke when” in real-world audio, supports both streaming and offline inference, and is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. It is a 100-million-parameter, 31-layer Transformer encoder with Rotary Positional Embeddings. Incoming 16 kHz single-channel audio is converted into 10-millisecond mel-spectrogram frames, downsampled by a factor of eight to an 80-millisecond encoder frame rate, and a Conv1D layer above the encoder upsamples predictions back to the 10-millisecond input resolution. The model outputs a tensor of per-speaker activity probabilities with shape T, 8, and its eight speaker channels are ordered by each speaker’s first arrival in the audio.

For streaming, the model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache and FIFO queue introduced in NVIDIA’s Streaming Sortformer work: the cache retains speaker information from earlier chunks so the first voice heard keeps its label, while the queue provides recent frame context for each processing step. The design requires no embeddings or clustering, and chunked inference places no fixed limit on audio duration.

A single checkpoint serves four recommended latency configurations: 0.32, 0.64, and 1.04 seconds, plus an offline-style 30.4-second input buffer. The card defines this latency as input buffer latency — chunk length plus right context, multiplied by 80 milliseconds — and notes that the figure excludes computational processing time. The checkpoint can run with a buffer as low as 80 milliseconds, though 0.32 seconds is the lowest recommended configuration, and output frame resolution is configurable in multiples of 10 milliseconds.

NVIDIA’s model card reports diarization error rate, speaker counting accuracy, and speaker counting mean absolute error against the diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 baseline, with overlapping speech included and a zero-second collar on every benchmark except CALLHOME-Part2, which uses a 0.25-second collar. On DIHARD III, the card reports a full-set error rate of 12.73 at the 30.4-second profile and 13.55 at 0.32 seconds, versus 19.09 and 19.85 for the baseline. On NOTSOFAR1 single-channel recordings it reports 11.00 versus 30.49 at the offline profile; on AMI Test SDM, 11.14 versus 21.42; on AliMeeting Test Near, 6.40 versus 11.57; and on CALLHOME-Part2, 9.10 versus 10.32. The card states that its AMI, AliMeeting, and NOTSOFAR1 scores were computed with forced-alignment reference labels and that results scored against different reference annotations are not directly comparable.

A speed table in the card reports real-time-factor speedup, defined as total audio duration divided by total processing time, of 1,340 in eager mode and 4,385 compiled at batch size one on the offline profile, measured on an RTX PRO 5000 at BF16 precision. At the 0.32-second profile, the corresponding figures are 12.5 and 54.

Baseten ran its own evaluation, also scoring error rate with overlapping speech included and no collar. It reports a 9.8 percent error rate on AISHELL-4 at the low latency profile against 27.2 percent for Streaming Sortformer v2.1, and says that moving from the 30-second offline profile to the 0.32-second ultra-low profile raises the error rate by only one to two points. Baseten reports the model outperformed Meta Muse Voice Transcribe on every dataset it tested, at even the ultra-low configuration, and lost to pyannote community-1 only on AMI.

The model card lists roughly 10,000 hours of real conversations (including Fisher English, the AMI and ICSI meeting corpora, VoxConverse, AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, the third DIHARD challenge, CALLHOME, NOTSOFAR1, the DISPLACE sets, licensed David AI recordings, and a pseudo-labeled YODAS-v2 subset) alongside 82,611 hours of multi-talker mixtures simulated with the FastMSS toolkit from about 28,000 hours of single-speaker recordings. Training initialized from a NEST self-supervised checkpoint and ran on eight nodes of eight A100-80GB GPUs in two stages: offline training on simulated data, followed by streaming fine-tuning on a combination of real and simulated audio. Use of the model is governed by the OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1.

Baseten exposes the model through three presets, each running on one RTX PRO 6000 behind a CUDA-graph engine built around NVIDIA’s NeMo streaming loop, according to its Model Library listing , which also describes the model as the successor to Streaming Sortformer v2.1. The Batch Diarization preset is an HTTP endpoint for recorded audio that returns speaker turns with a per-request latency profile. Streaming Diarization is a WebSocket endpoint for live audio that carries speaker identity across a conversation without re-clustering. Streaming Diarized Transcription pairs the diarizer with NVIDIA’s Parakeet V2 speech recognition model, a 600-million-parameter system, and returns speaker-tagged words with timings, per-speaker partials, and overlap flags. Baseten says this preset feeds per-speaker activity vectors directly into Parakeet’s initial encoder layers so overlapped speech is transcribed in a single pass, with speaker labels final on arrival and committed words never revised.

Baseten reports that one RTX PRO 6000 sustains more than 500 concurrent hour-long diarization streams at the 1.04-second profile, 200 streams at the 0.32-second profile, and 190 hour-long streams when transcription is added, while the batch preset processes 200 six-minute audio files per minute. Using identical files and hardware, Baseten reports that its optimized preset delivered roughly 1.35 times higher batch throughput than the NVIDIA reference setup it tested, under k6-generated load inside the cluster with a one-stream control on an idle replica.

Baseten also says the model’s per-speaker activity signal, tracked in 10-millisecond increments, can drive voice activity detection, speaker-specific end-of-turn detection, and turn-taking and interruption handling, responding in roughly 300 milliseconds on ultra-low latency settings.

Nemotron 3 Diarization is available on Hugging Face under the repository nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization and in Baseten’s Model Library, with NeMo Framework v3.0 integration and support for NVIDIA Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell GPUs.

extraction.body: Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year. The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials. A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access. More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry. The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA. Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out. This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors. The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest. TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff . It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch after publication: “DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively. We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected. We will update the public when more information is available.” When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said. While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE. The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work. Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software. The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit. A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023. Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media. A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment. One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status . The user groups also include several employees associated with ChatGPT access, including senior DHS officials, as well as other groups associated with investigations into the China-backed hacking groups known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon. Researchers and public information advocates say that the exposed data could provide valuable leads for investigations into alleged abuses by the Trump administration, such as identifying email addresses of agents that can be used in public records requests under the Freedom of Information Act. “Email addresses and phone numbers are indispensable tools for FOIA researchers, often making the difference between a vague records request that gets stonewalled and one that gets results,” said Ryan Shapiro, the executive director of transparency nonprofit Property of the People. “Given the Trump administration’s contempt for even basic transparency, the need for such tools is urgent,” said Shapiro. DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best said that the exposed Homeland Security data will be a “catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, Congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests.” Zack Whittaker is the security editor at TechCrunch. He also authors the weekly cybersecurity newsletter, this week in security . He can be reached via encrypted message at zackwhittaker.1337 on Signal. You can also contact him by email, or to verify outreach, at [email protected] .

The hacker claimed to have extracted the data from the Okta single sign-on (SSO) system used by DHS employees and contractors to log into a central network, and the hacker left a note saying, "They have our information, so it is fair for us to have theirs." Distributed Denial of Secrets hosted the leak in a database named Icepick and shared it through a website hosted by Distributed Denial of Secrets, and the BBC said the Wednesday leak marked the third time in recent weeks a government agency had been targeted by leaks or hacks. Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets, said the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability," and Best added that the leak identified the officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations. The Department of Peace pointed directly at actions by ICE agents for the groups work to hack DHS records, and a spokesperson wrote on Wednesday, "On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat'." Okta responded to the claims by saying, "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised," and the BBC reported that a representative of the DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A hacker using the name "Department of Peace" stole personal information on about 40,000 employees of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and posted it online, TechCrunch reported on Oct. 28 local time.

The leaked information included names, titles, email addresses, mobile phone numbers and office locations, and the data also included information on border and immigration enforcement officers, cybersecurity staff and senior officials.

The hacker claimed to have extracted the data from the Okta single sign-on (SSO) system used by DHS employees and contractors to log into a central network, and the hacker left a note saying, "They have our information, so it is fair for us to have theirs."

More than half of the leaked records, about 21,000 entries, involved U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) employees, and the data also included information on 10,000 employees of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit.
Okta said there was no evidence its data or systems had been compromised, and the leak was described as the second leak DHS has suffered this year.

Distributed Denial of Secrets hosted the leak in a database named Icepick and shared it through a website hosted by Distributed Denial of Secrets, and the BBC said the Wednesday leak marked the third time in recent weeks a government agency had been targeted by leaks or hacks. Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets, said the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability," and Best added that the leak identified the officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations. The Department of Peace pointed directly at actions by ICE agents for the groups work to hack DHS records, and a spokesperson wrote on Wednesday, "On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat'."

Okta responded to the claims by saying, "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised," and the BBC reported that a representative of the DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The leaked information also included dozens of previously unknown operation names, the agents that led and worked on those operations, and some of the technology they used in their work, including tech provided by Cellbrite and Palantir.

extraction.body: Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year. The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials. A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access. More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry. The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA. Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out. This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors. The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. “PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display.

Users can scroll a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag slides from one presentation to another and double-tap a window to fill the screen.
macOS translates touches into clicks, so many existing apps work with Touch at launch, Apple said.

Pixelmator Pro, Logic Pro and Final Cut Pro gain Touch controls through Apple Creator Studio.
Apple said a redesigned hinge adds stability when the screen is touched, and video stabilisation smooths the camera feed when Touch is used during a video call.

extraction.body: On October 28, 2026, Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, the first Mac ever to feature a touchscreen. The new tandem OLED panel replaces the previous Mini-LED display, offering up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. Featuring the M5 Pro or M5 Max, Dynamic Island, and up to 24 hours of battery life, the device goes on sale starting November 6, with prices in the U.S. starting at $2,899. With PROLED XDR, Apple is introducing a new designation for the displays on its Pro laptops. Technically, it’s a tandem OLED panel: Two stacked light-emitting layers work together to produce greater brightness and more uniform illumination than a single OLED panel could achieve. Apple cites up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness in SDR and HDR, as well as a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. By comparison, the previous Liquid Retina XDR display with Mini-LED backlighting achieved 1,600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a contrast ratio of 1,000,000:1. In addition, there is a wider color gamut that now covers Adobe RGB in addition to P3; both color spaces are included in a single preset profile. For video professionals, the Rec. 2020 coverage of over 80 percent is likely to be of particular interest. The variable refresh rate ranges from 10 to 120 Hz; depending on the content, the system automatically switches between power-saving mode and smooth display. Anti-glare nano-textured glass remains available as an optional extra. 42 years after the introduction of the first Macintosh, Apple is bringing touch control to a Mac screen. According to Apple, the touch sensor is embedded directly into the panel rather than being an additional layer on top, which is designed to reduce response time. Scrolling, zooming with a two-finger gesture, and moving windows work as expected; macOS automatically translates touch inputs into clicks in existing apps. Things get even more interesting for creatives: In Pixelmator Pro, you can draw directly on the screen; in Logic Pro, musicians can play a virtual multi-finger keyboard; and Final Cut Pro users can mark cut points with a tap. App developers can also test iOS and iPadOS apps for touch compatibility directly on the MacBook Pro display. A redesigned hinge mechanism is intended to keep the display stable when tapped, preventing the screen from wobbling. For those who’ve been following the pre-release coverage: We had already announced this exact device in advance as a MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen ; Apple has now confirmed the rumors with its own name and release timeline. Dynamic Island, previously seen on the iPhone, is now coming to the Mac. It serves as a launch point for Spotlight, displays Live Activities, and acts as the docking point for Siri AI. Users can use it to ask questions, answer a call, or control music playback without moving the mouse pointer. Anyone already familiar with the iPhone 18 Pro —on which Dynamic Island has been running since September—will recognize this interaction pattern. On the software side, the MacBook Pro runs macOS 27 “Golden Gate.” Siri AI is said to be significantly more conversational and able to access personal context from messages, emails, and photos, though with daily usage limits for features that run on Apple’s servers. In Safari, Apple Intelligence automatically organizes tabs by topic, and in the future, shortcuts can be easily created using descriptions. Under the hood are the M5 Pro and M5 Max, which Apple claims are the most powerful chips ever in a Pro notebook. Both feature a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core, designed to speed up AI tasks such as running a coding assistant locally. According to Apple, the M5 Max allows language models with several hundred billion parameters to run entirely on the device—a claim aimed primarily at AI developers and VFX studios. While the chip generation is familiar, the new chassis comes as a surprise: The 14-inch model now weighs 1.36 kilograms, while the 16-inch model weighs 1.81 kilograms. According to Apple, this is made possible by the space-saving design of the OLED panel compared to Mini-LED; the 14-inch model weighs about 225 grams less than its predecessor. Thanks to narrower bezels, the screen sizes have increased slightly to 14.2 and 16.3 inches, respectively. Battery life is expected to remain at up to 24 hours despite the thinner enclosure, and a redesigned thermal management system is intended to efficiently dissipate heat away from the display. A new feature is dedicated audio tuning for use with the lid closed while connected to an external monitor. For video production, there’s support for Genlock, which synchronizes the display’s refresh rate with the recording from a compatible camera—a feature that’s likely to be of particular interest on virtual production sets. The iMac with the M6 chip and the 2026 iPad mini —featuring an OLED display for the first time—are also part of this week’s product lineup. The fact that the PROLED-XDR model is now launching anyway—and sits right alongside a standard, non-touch M6 MacBook Pro in the lineup—shows just how cautiously Apple is proceeding. passages: Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the first time on Mac

The world’s best pro laptop now features an industry-leading tandem OLED display, an intuitive Touch experience, blazing-fast M5 Pro and M5 Max performance and AI capabilities, and up to 24 hours of battery life, all in a thinner, lighter design

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display , featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology that delivers game-changing front-of-screen performance. Available in 14- and 16-inch models, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display offers a visual experience unlike any other, transforming pro workflows with up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for exceptional detail, a 120Hz variable refresh rate, and a wider color gamut covering both P3 and Adobe RGB for brilliant colors. The new MacBook Pro also introduces intuitive Touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time, opening up a whole new dimension for pros to interact with their content, from manipulating 3D models to playing musical instruments onscreen. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI. 2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes. 3 Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple’s most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and now up to 16TB of blazing-fast storage, the new MacBook Pro delivers speed and capability for the most demanding workflows. An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio. And Thunderbolt 5 and a wide array of connectivity, a 12MP Center Stage camera, studio-quality mics, and the power of macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI complete the MacBook Pro experience. 2 It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.

“The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac,” said Johny Srouji, Apple’s chief hardware officer. “PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of. And with the magic of Touch coming to MacBook Pro, combined with the game-changing performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, we’ve created a whole new way for pros to interact with their content, taking their workflows to a completely new level. The new MacBook Pro is the result of the deep integration between Apple silicon, hardware, and software, and there’s simply nothing else like it.”
PROLED XDR: The World’s Best Display in a Pro Laptop

The new MacBook Pro debuts the PROLED XDR display, which uses tandem OLED technology and advances it with breakthrough innovations in every layer, advanced algorithms in the display engine, and a state-of-the-art factory calibration process to deliver Extreme Dynamic Range (XDR) and stunning visual fidelity. With exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors, PROLED XDR offers the ultimate front-of-screen performance, enabling a new level of visual acuity and precision for content creators, photographers, colorists, and designers who need a reference-caliber display on the go.

PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display, delivering true-to-life color and unparalleled brightness and contrast. The PROLED XDR display offers tandem OLED technology unlike any other, with deep innovations in its layers that keep brightness and grayscale uniform across the entire display, while minimizing internal reflections common in traditional OLED designs. It’s all backed by advanced algorithms in the display engine that precisely control each pixel in real time, plus a meticulous manufacturing process and precise calibration of every panel for consistency from display to display.

PROLED XDR offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, allowing specular highlights to shine with stunning intensity. And through optimizations in the tandem OLED panel and custom compensation techniques, combined with precise control of light across the display, the PROLED XDR display achieves an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, so even the deepest shadows reveal incredible detail, bringing HDR content remarkably close to reality.
The Ultimate Display for Color-Critical Workflows

PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB — critical for workflows in photography and design — along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges. This results in more than 80 percent Rec. 2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading. Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets. Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them. With the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, pros have a portable reference display on the go.

With up to 2000 nits peak SDR brightness, combined with a state-of-the-art antireflective coating, the display is easy to read even in bright lighting conditions. For even greater visibility, the nano-texture option — now precisely etched into the cover glass — further reduces reflections and glare to eliminate distractions while maintaining an excellent viewing experience.

With breakthrough tandem OLED technology, extreme brightness, and extraordinary contrast, along with a super-wide color gamut, PROLED XDR is truly the world’s best laptop display, giving pros an unparalleled visual experience and setting a whole new bar for the industry.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.

Apple apps are optimized for the new MacBook Pro, and many existing apps work with Touch right away, because macOS automatically translates touches into clicks. Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch. And a wide range of third-party apps that pros rely on every day will also take advantage of Touch on the new MacBook Pro, bringing new ways to interact with their favorite tools and workflows. These include everyday productivity and collaboration apps like Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook; powerful creative tools for photo and video editing like Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve; 3D modeling and animation apps like Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, and Shapr3D; along with music apps like Algoriddim djay Pro. 4

The Dynamic Island comes to the Mac, serving as the new home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI, where users can quickly search for anything on their MacBook Pro, access real-time updates, or take advantage of Siri AI. 1 Just like on iPhone, the Dynamic Island provides a quick, intuitive way to see and interact with important information. Users can ask a question, pick up a phone call, or control music — all within easy reach. With Live Activities, users can now get timely updates at a glance, and can accept an AirDrop request or pause a song with a tap of their finger.

The new MacBook Pro is thinner and significantly lighter for even better portability. The 14-inch MacBook Pro now weighs half a pound less at 3 pounds, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs just 4 pounds — 0.7 pounds lighter than before. 5 Both models feature a slimmer design enabled by OLED’s more efficient display stack, with the 16-inch model nearly a millimeter thinner and the 14-inch model half a millimeter thinner.

With slimmer display borders, the 16-inch display grows to 16.3 inches, while the 14-inch display delivers a more portable 14.2-inch design. 6 And a completely redesigned thermal architecture enables the same incredible sustained performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, even in a lighter design, while redirecting warm air away from the display.
M5 Pro and M5 Max: Game‑Changing Pro Performance and On-Device AI

The new MacBook Pro features M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple’s most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop. Both deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance, along with faster unified memory, giving users blazing speed for the most demanding workflows. M5 Pro offers game-changing performance for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects, accelerating everything from compiling code and running AI tasks to sequencing DNA and editing multiple streams of 8K ProRes video. M5 Max is built for users who want to push the limits even further, including 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers. With M5 Max, pros can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device and accelerate intense workflows across detailed visual effects, 3D animation projects, film scores, and 8K video post-production.

A powerful Neural Accelerator built into each GPU core lets users speed through AI workloads like running a coding agent with an on-device LLM. And users are able to power through advanced graphics-intensive tasks like rendering a complex scene in Cinema 4D with Redshift. M5 Pro and M5 Max each feature a GPU with enhanced shader cores and a third-generation ray-tracing engine, delivering more photorealistic lighting and faster renders for 3D modeling. Dynamic Caching optimizes on-chip memory to significantly increase GPU utilization, driving huge performance boosts for apps like Blender and Unreal Engine, along with AAA games.

The industry-leading six-speaker audio system in the new MacBook Pro features an all-new woofer design that provides 50 percent deeper bass and all-new tweeters that shape sound dispersion for remarkable clarity. Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos wraps users in immersive sound for music and movies, and studio-quality mics deliver clean, clear audio for calls, recordings, and voice commands. And for the first time, dedicated audio tuning for closed-lid use delivers exceptional sound quality when MacBook Pro is connected to an external display, so users can enjoy a premium audio experience however they work.

The new MacBook Pro packs features for the most demanding users. The PROLED XDR display offers calibration and industry-standard reference modes in a portable form factor, making MacBook Pro an indispensable tool for filmmaking, design, and even medical imaging. 7 And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.

The new MacBook Pro includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. In addition to the PROLED XDR display, it supports up to three external displays with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max. Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience. With its fast-charge capability, MacBook Pro can charge up to 50 percent in just 30 minutes. 3 In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16TB.

The new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27. In addition to Touch built for macOS 27, MacBook Pro includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across apps; and an expansive set of improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item. Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.

Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Pros can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. Features users already rely on get even better with improvements to performance and search. Refinements to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and the Environment

The new MacBook Pro was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The new MacBook Pro is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.

passages: The 14-inch MacBook Pro with Apple’s PROLED XDR tandem OLED display starts at $2,899 in the US, according to MacRumors , and ships from Friday 6 November 2026.
Apple announced the laptop in a press release on 28 October 2026 and said it brings Touch to the Mac for the first time.
Thinner display borders take the screens to 14.2 and 16.3 inches.
The M5 Pro version drives up to three external displays and the M5 Max up to four.
Fast charging takes the battery to 50 per cent in 30 minutes, and the six-speaker sound system has a new woofer design that Apple said gives 50 per cent deeper bass.
Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 run on an Apple-designed N1 wireless chip.
The panel covers both the P3 and Adobe RGB colour spaces, with more than 80 per cent coverage of Rec.
A nano-texture option etched into the cover glass cuts reflections and glare.
Apple said the display reaches up to 2000 nits of peak brightness for HDR and SDR content, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and a refresh rate that varies between 10Hz and 120Hz.
Users can scroll a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag slides from one presentation to another and double-tap a window to fill the screen.
macOS translates touches into clicks, so many existing apps work with Touch at launch, Apple said.

Apps that Apple lists as taking advantage of Touch include Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, along with Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, Shapr3D and Algoriddim djay Pro.
Pixelmator Pro, Logic Pro and Final Cut Pro gain Touch controls through Apple Creator Studio.
Apple said a redesigned hinge adds stability when the screen is touched, and video stabilisation smooths the camera feed when Touch is used during a video call.
The laptops run macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

Apple apps are optimized for the new MacBook Pro, and many existing apps work with Touch right away, because macOS automatically translates touches into clicks. Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch. extraction.body: On October 28, 2026, Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, the first Mac ever to feature a touchscreen. The new tandem OLED panel replaces the previous Mini-LED display, offering up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. Featuring the M5 Pro or M5 Max, Dynamic Island, and up to 24 hours of battery life, the device goes on sale starting November 6, with prices in the U.S. starting at $2,899. With PROLED XDR, Apple is introducing a new designation for the displays on its Pro laptops. Technically, it’s a tandem OLED panel: Two stacked light-emitting layers work together to produce greater brightness and more uniform illumination than a single OLED panel could achieve. Apple cites up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness in SDR and HDR, as well as a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. By comparison, the previous Liquid Retina XDR display with Mini-LED backlighting achieved 1,600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a contrast ratio of 1,000,000:1. In addition, there is a wider color gamut that now covers Adobe RGB in addition to P3; both color spaces are included in a single preset profile. For video professionals, the Rec. 2020 coverage of over 80 percent is likely to be of particular interest. The variable refresh rate ranges from 10 to 120 Hz; depending on the content, the system automatically switches between power-saving mode and smooth display. Anti-glare nano-textured glass remains available as an optional extra. 42 years after the introduction of the first Macintosh, Apple is bringing touch control to a Mac screen. According to Apple, the touch sensor is embedded directly into the panel rather than being an additional layer on top, which is designed to reduce response time. Scrolling, zooming with a two-finger gesture, and moving windows work as expected; macOS automatically translates touch inputs into clicks in existing apps. Things get even more interesting for creatives: In Pixelmator Pro, you can draw directly on the screen; in Logic Pro, musicians can play a virtual multi-finger keyboard; and Final Cut Pro users can mark cut points with a tap. App developers can also test iOS and iPadOS apps for touch compatibility directly on the MacBook Pro display. A redesigned hinge mechanism is intended to keep the display stable when tapped, preventing the screen from wobbling. For those who’ve been following the pre-release coverage: We had already announced this exact device in advance as a MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen ; Apple has now confirmed the rumors with its own name and release timeline. Dynamic Island, previously seen on the iPhone, is now coming to the Mac. It serves as a launch point for Spotlight, displays Live Activities, and acts as the docking point for Siri AI. Users can use it to ask questions, answer a call, or control music playback without moving the mouse pointer. Anyone already familiar with the iPhone 18 Pro —on which Dynamic Island has been running since September—will recognize this interaction pattern. On the software side, the MacBook Pro runs macOS 27 “Golden Gate.” Siri AI is said to be significantly more conversational and able to access personal context from messages, emails, and photos, though with daily usage limits for features that run on Apple’s servers. In Safari, Apple Intelligence automatically organizes tabs by topic, and in the future, shortcuts can be easily created using descriptions. Under the hood are the M5 Pro and M5 Max, which Apple claims are the most powerful chips ever in a Pro notebook. Both feature a Neural Accelerator in each GPU core, designed to speed up AI tasks such as running a coding assistant locally. According to Apple, the M5 Max allows language models with several hundred billion parameters to run entirely on the device—a claim aimed primarily at AI developers and VFX studios. While the chip generation is familiar, the new chassis comes as a surprise: The 14-inch model now weighs 1.36 kilograms, while the 16-inch model weighs 1.81 kilograms. According to Apple, this is made possible by the space-saving design of the OLED panel compared to Mini-LED; the 14-inch model weighs about 225 grams less than its predecessor. Thanks to narrower bezels, the screen sizes have increased slightly to 14.2 and 16.3 inches, respectively. Battery life is expected to remain at up to 24 hours despite the thinner enclosure, and a redesigned thermal management system is intended to efficiently dissipate heat away from the display. The laptop features three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. With the M5 Pro, up to three external displays can be used in addition to the built-in screen; with the M5 Max, the number increases to four. RAM capacity goes up to 128 GB, and flash storage up to 16 TB—both significantly more than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip , released at the same time, which lacks a touchscreen and features a Mini-LED display. The six-speaker system features new woofers for 50 percent more bass and redesigned tweeters. A new feature is dedicated audio tuning for use with the lid closed while connected to an external monitor. For video production, there’s support for Genlock, which synchronizes the display’s refresh rate with the recording from a compatible camera—a feature that’s likely to be of particular interest on virtual production sets. The exact RAM limit depends on the selected chip configuration; Apple specifies 128 GB only for the top-of-the-line M5 Max model. All information is based on manufacturer specifications; alternative configurations can be customized individually through Apple. In the U.S., the 14-inch model with the M5 Pro starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch model with the M5 Pro starts at $3,399. With the M5 Max, prices are $4,499 for the smaller model and $4,799 for the larger one. Apple did not specify concrete euro prices for Germany in the press release, but they should become available when sales begin on the Apple Online Store . Experience shows that German prices are higher than the straight dollar exchange rate due to VAT and rounding, but this can only be reliably confirmed once the German pricing page goes live. Pre-orders have been available since October 28 via the Apple Store app and apple.com, with shipments beginning Friday, November 6, 2026, initially in 30 countries. Those who opt for the more affordable, non-touch option will find an alternative in the MacBook Pro with the M6 chip —unveiled at the same time—which offers the new display at no extra cost. The iMac with the M6 chip and the 2026 iPad mini —featuring an OLED display for the first time—are also part of this week’s product lineup. For years, the idea of a touchscreen on the MacBook Pro sounded like a rumor that would never come true; Apple had publicly described touch on the Mac as impractical on multiple occasions. The fact that the PROLED-XDR model is now launching anyway—and sits right alongside a standard, non-touch M6 MacBook Pro in the lineup—shows just how cautiously Apple is proceeding. Those with no interest in touch don’t have to switch and won’t pay any extra for it. So who will really benefit from this device? The strongest arguments come not from the touchscreen, but from the display itself: 2,000 nits of SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio are figures no laptop display has ever achieved, and Adobe RGB in addition to P3 is a real step forward for photographers and graphic designers. Whether the touchscreen offers any real benefit in everyday use depends heavily on your own workflow. Those who work in Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, or Final Cut will likely take to it quickly. Those who primarily type and click with a mouse on their Mac, on the other hand, are getting a significantly more expensive display whose additional feature goes unused. The premium over a comparably equipped MacBook Pro with the M6 ranges roughly between $400 and $900, depending on the configuration. This isn’t a must-buy, but rather a clear niche product: content creators, colorists, and musicians who use the display as a tool will find this to be their best Mac display yet. For everyone else, the M6 MacBook Pro remains the more sensible choice. PROLED XDR is Apple’s new name for the tandem OLED display in the MacBook Pro. It replaces the previous Mini-LED display, called Liquid Retina XDR, and, according to Apple, offers up to 2,000 nits of brightness and a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1. Yes, it’s the first MacBook Pro—and the first Mac ever—with a touchscreen. The touch sensor is built directly into the display and supports gestures such as scrolling, zooming, and dragging. Yes, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, introduced on October 27, 2026, remains in the lineup without a touchscreen and with a Mini-LED display, at a lower starting price. In the U.S., the 14-inch model with the M5 Pro starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch model with the M5 Max starts at $4,799. Apple has not yet released German prices in euros. Pre-orders have been open since October 28, 2026, via the Apple Online Store, and shipping begins on November 6, 2026, in 30 countries, including Germany. passages: Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop on October 28, 2026, and the price tag landed as loudly as the feature.
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch, according to Ars Technica’s launch coverage .
Both sizes use Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and both go on sale November 6, 2026.
The gap between the two sizes is exactly $500, or roughly 17% on top of the smaller model’s base price.
Apple has not published a wider configuration list in the material we verified, so those two numbers are the only prices we can state with confidence.
The takeaway: Apple has crossed a line it held for years, and it did so at the top of its price range.
Whether that bet works depends on facts the company has not yet shown, from battery life to repair costs to how well macOS handles fingers.

This analysis covers what Apple confirmed, what it left open, how the pricing compares with the rest of the market, and what the touchscreen MacBook Pro means for buyers, developers and rival laptop makers.
BNN Bloomberg’s report on the first touchscreen laptops arriving amid a product blitz placed the launch inside a busy stretch for Apple, and that context matters for pricing.
When a company launches several products in a short window, it usually prices the newest halo item high and lets cheaper models absorb the volume.
A $2,899 entry point reads as a halo price, aimed at buyers who already pay for top-end Pro hardware.
Retailers and resellers face a trickier picture.
Investors will watch the November 6 launch window and the following quarter for signs of whether premium Mac demand holds.
We will track the broader hardware picture in our hardware coverage hub as sales data arrives.
For now, the sensible stance is interest without haste.
Past launches, from the first Retina MacBook Pro to the mini-LED displays, followed a similar path.
Coverage names John Ternus as the Apple executive who unveiled the touchscreen MacBooks, and identifies him as the company’s CEO.
OLED panels draw different power than LCD panels depending on what is on screen, and a touch layer adds its own overhead.
If you plan to buy on November 6, wait for reviews that run the same workload on the old and new models.
Pricing tells you who Apple expects to buy first.
The gaps in the announcement are as useful to know as the specs.
Several details that buyers will want before spending $2,899 or more are not in the verified record.

extraction.body: Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop on October 28, 2026, and the price tag landed as loudly as the feature. The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch, according to Ars Technica’s launch coverage . Both sizes use Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and both go on sale November 6, 2026. For a company that spent more than a decade steering Mac owners toward the keyboard and trackpad, this is a real reversal. We tracked the build-up in our earlier look at the Pro and tell launch expectations , and the final product matches the broad outline. This analysis covers what Apple confirmed, what it left open, how the pricing compares with the rest of the market, and what the touchscreen MacBook Pro means for buyers, developers and rival laptop makers.
