Senior Editor / Computers and Gaming Hardware Surpassed only by the iPhone Duo , this year’s most anticipated Apple announcement is its launch of both a 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen display — the company’s last-to-the-party use of both technologies in one of its laptops. And despite the awful name, it’s more than just a fancy new display. It’s really a complete design overhaul that, at least on paper, brings its feature set up to the front of the class for professional content creation, albeit with the same processor options and ports as the other MacBook Pros. Aside from a screen that brings its capabilities more in line with the Studio Display XDR , the new model adds: It doesn’t come cheap, though; as predicted, you pay a $400 premium over the standard models. The 14-inch M5 Pro model starts at $2,899 compared with $2,499 for the same non-OLED version, and the M5 Max model begins at $4,499 compared with $4,099. If you want to upgrade to 16TB, you have to bump to the M5 Max — that’s a minimum buy-in of $11,499 with only 36GB of memory. Preorders started on Wednesday, and systems are slated to start shipping Nov. 6. One of the most popular changes won’t be the whizzy features, but the drop in weight to 3 pounds for the 14-inch model (down from 3.4 pounds) and to 4 pounds (down from 4.7 pounds) for the 16-inch. Also, while Apple updated its sound system to deliver better bass and incorporated Dolby Atmos support to its spatial audio, one of the more notable enhancements is the claimed improvements to the sound when the MacBook is closed. A lot of the traditional advantages of OLED over alternatives like IPS with array backlights — such as a wider color gamut and true blacks — are less pronounced than they used to be. That’s even more true for the current MacBook Pro’s mini-LED-backlit Liquid Retina XDR screens: They already deliver excellent deep blacks and 100% P3 gamut coverage, along with great color accuracy sufficient for prosumer creative work. But the PROLED XDR screen sounds top-notch. While I take Apple’s claim of a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio with 10,000,000 grains of salt — the arithmetic ratio of peak brightness to minimum black isn’t really meaningful, especially beyond about a million — the display has an expanded gamut that covers the Adobe RGB color space and more of Rec. 2020, a space for mastering video. The latter is still only 80%, but at the moment, that’s the best you can get in a laptop display. Peak brightness is also similar to the desktop display at 2,000 nits. As with the current screens, though, you can set the SDR brightness only up to 1,000 nits; above that, it’s automated to compensate only for bright sunlight. That can get frustrating for people like me who find auto- brightness distracting. The display can do 1,000 nits full screen in both SDR and HDR, though. Microsoft’s recently shipped Surface Laptop Ultra also hits 2,000 nits, the first Windows laptop that does, but uses mini-LED. Oddly, Apple still quotes a 1-nit minimum brightness spec, similar to its mini-LED screens, though OLED’s native minimum is a lot lower: Theoretically, it’s zero, but professional colorimeters have measured it a lot lower. That may be because Apple has adopted it as a standard, and possibly clamped it, to tonally match its mini-LED models. Apple also refers to its panel technology generically as “tandem OLED,” which is a little annoying, since there is a raft of tandem OLED types. But it is “state of the art!” There are a couple of potential disappointments, though. For one, the battery life is unchanged. While the MacBook Pro’s battery life has always been good, it’s clear that the OLED display didn’t provide any power savings, or at least savings that weren’t spent elsewhere in the system. Touch looks like the biggest mixed bag, though. The hardware is only a small aspect of the implementation; operating system interfaces like those of iOS and iPadOS are built around considerations like your finger is bigger and fatter than a cursor. Simply porting the mobile interfaces to a laptop isn’t necessarily a solution, either. We use laptops in part because a hardware keyboard is sometimes the best input choice, and even navigating the mobile devices via touch can get annoying, so those interfaces don’t necessarily translate optimally. The point is, a lot is riding on how Apple has adapted MacOS for touch. For instance, the Touch Bar floundered in part because it felt grafted on rather than integral to the OS’ interface, as well as arguably superfluous. And since Apple didn’t launch the capability with MacOS 27 at its developer conference, WWDC , this year, it sounds like the applications will be behind. That’s not something you beta test on a pro-level production system. Pros rely heavily on muscle memory. It should really have launched with a MacBook Air. Plus, to adapt to touchscreen use, Apple had to stiffen the hinge — poking the screen makes that necessary — and add image stabilization to the webcam in case you poke the screen during video calls. Apple seemed like it was really stretching to find meaningful uses for touch. Playing piano on a screen that forces your hand to an awkward angle? No thanks. The one application that sounded like it might be OK was for developers to simulate mobile app interfaces. I was also kind of hoping for increased refresh rates beyond 120Hz or the ability to manually set it above 60Hz. Apple seems to position ProMotion as a power-saving technology rather than for gaming. Apple also seems to think 60fps is a great frame rate, so it’s not surprising. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

story.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro hands-on: OLED looks great on a Mac

facts.text: The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models.
Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps.
Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one.
Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface.
That’s why it’s just a MacBook Pro variant and not an entirely new product line.
And while MacBook Pro hinges are pretty solid, yes, you can make it wobble pretty easily with some firm taps toward the top of the screen.
While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly.

Apple is trying to address this, at least slightly, by magnifying some controls when you poke at them — like the red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons in the top left corner of windows to close, minimize, and maximize an app.
On first impression, at least, the touchscreen doesn’t seem likely to revolutionize the MacBook.

I’m looking forward to spending more time with the new MacBook Pro, but for right now, it seems to follow in the lineup’s existing tradition: impressively high-end components like an outstanding OLED panel, but a very steep price to match.
Though after well over a decade of speculation and back-and-forth, you’d be forgiven for being surprised that the touchscreen thing actually finally happened.
But while it’s not about the touchscreen capability for me, I was impressed by the OLED screen itself—and I’m quite the display snob, if I’m being honest.
The peak brightness, absolute blacks, well-balanced color, and dynamic range were genuinely remarkable.

When the credible reports emerged that the MacBook Pro would get a touchscreen, I imagined a convertible with Apple Pencil support—something you could use as a large iPad or drawing tablet, essentially.

As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production. The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver. Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini . The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip. The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says. The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip. “The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities

M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.

The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.

There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.

Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
The latest news and updates, direct from Apple.

extraction.body: Additionally, the N1 chip brings Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage. There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage. It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers. The M6 iMac should see up to double SSD read/write performance compared to the M4 model, too. The previous entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro had the M5, so that one is just stepping up a single generation. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. In addition to the M6 chip, both computers now have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity (that means Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6). The iMac is now configurable with up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, while the MacBook Pro still lacks an Ethernet port. There are no outward design changes to either device; they both look exactly the same as their immediate predecessors. The iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port version, or $1,699 for the four-port version. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999. Preorders start October 28, and they ship November 6. This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot.

Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip .
This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely).
The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac.

Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini .

Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage. There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage. It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers. The M6 iMac should see up to double SSD read/write performance compared to the M4 model, too. The previous entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro had the M5, so that one is just stepping up a single generation. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. In addition to the M6 chip, both computers now have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity (that means Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6). The iMac is now configurable with up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, while the MacBook Pro still lacks an Ethernet port. There are no outward design changes to either device; they both look exactly the same as their immediate predecessors. The iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port version, or $1,699 for the four-port version. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999. Preorders start October 28, and they ship November 6. Apple has rolled out a new 24-inch iMac and an entry-level MacBook Pro with a 14-inch screen, marking key updates in an end-to-end overhaul of the company’s computer line. The new iMac and MacBook Pro, unveiled on Oct 27 , are visually similar to their predecessors – with the main changes happening internally. Both machines now include the M6 chip, which debuted in the Mac mini in September. The iMac is moving from an M4 processor, while the MacBook Pro received the M5 in 2025 . The updates represent a second day of Apple announcements this week, with the company rolling out a revamped iPad mini on Oct 26 with a new screen and water resistance. Apple will cap the launches on Oct 28 with its first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, Bloomberg News has reported. The updated iMac and low-end MacBook Pro become available for pre-orders on Oct 28 and will arrive beginning Nov 6, Apple said, matching the new iPad mini. The new iMac starts at US$1,499 (S$1,920), while the MacBook Pro begins at US$1,999. Apple said the M6 chip makes the iMac five times faster than the prior model from 2024 for artificial intelligence, while the new MacBook Pro is 30% speedier than its predecessor for graphics. The company continues to sell higher-end M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros, which have more advanced main processing and graphics cores compared with the entry M6 machines. The updated 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac also include Bluetooth 6 and Wi-Fi 7, while the laptop gets faster charging. Both machines go on sale Nov. 6 after pre-orders open on Oct 28 . The new Macs come as part of a slew of changes to the company’s computer line. Beyond the push into touchscreen displays, Apple is preparing a refreshed MacBook Neo and MacBook Air for the first half of 2027 . The company is also working on a redesigned low-end MacBook Pro and the release of its first M7, M7 Pro and M7 Max chips in 2027. It is planning an M7 Ultra and a new Mac Studio in 2028. Apple’s overhauled MacBook Pro with a touchscreen – coming on Oct 28 – will include a lighter and slightly thinner design, slimmer bezels around the display and OLED technology, Bloomberg reported.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.

Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.

All configurations are available to order from Amazon .

sources.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar?
It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it.
Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd
I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.

LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

passages: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.
It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays.
John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X:
We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.
Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon .
Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration.
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF
The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
You can find Apple’s press release for the new machines here . All configurations are available to order from Amazon .

sources.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

extraction.body: Apple today announced a new high-end MacBook Pro , which is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The new device has a PROLED XDR display that supports touch gestures, and a glowing rear Apple logo. Pricing on the ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Apple says the ‌MacBook Pro‌ has the "world's best display in a pro laptop." The PROLED display uses tandem OLED paired with advanced algorithms in the display engine and factory calibration for "exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors." The display offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, along with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. An antireflective coating cuts down on glare in bright lighting conditions, and there is an option to order the new ‌MacBook Pro‌ with a nano-texture display. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. There is no more notch, with Apple instead adding a small Dynamic Island that takes up less space. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ houses Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Like on the iPhone, it offers a quick way to see and interact with important information. Smaller bezels mean the 16-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ display is now 16.3 inches in size, while the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ is now 14.2 inches. The new ‌MacBook Pro‌ uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the ‌MacBook Pro‌ models announced back in March, but there is a redesigned thermal architecture that directs warm air away from the display. There is support for up to 128GB of unified memory, and a new six-speaker sound system with 50 percent deeper bass. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe , and a headphone jack. The new machines support up to four external displays and come with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. story.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display

facts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar?
It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it.
Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd
I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:
All configurations are available to order from Amazon .
LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Memory configurations top out where they did in previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16TB—if you can afford it.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.

Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.

The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016.

The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.

The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.

Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.

The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel.

The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well).

The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors.

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variants offer 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 14-inch MacBook Pro features a 14.2-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3024 times; 1986 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 22 hours of video streaming and 14 hours of wireless web browsing. Both use a 72.6Wh battery and support fast charging with a 96W or higher USB PD power source.Connectivity options include three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, a MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip. The M5 Pro model supports up to three external displays, while the M5 Max variant can connect up to four.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 16-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 16-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The M5 Pro features an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, while the M5 Max is available with an 18-core CPU and either a 32-core or 40-core GPU. sources.title: Apple launches its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, from $2,899 - The Next Web
passages: Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

coreStoryFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip.
Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks.
Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website.
The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900.
The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip.
Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks.
Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.

contextFacts.text: Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

sources.title: Apple launches new MacBook Pro with touchscreen and OLED — starts at $2,899 - Tom's Hardware
passages: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variants offer 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 14-inch MacBook Pro features a 14.2-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3024 times; 1986 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 22 hours of video streaming and 14 hours of wireless web browsing. Both use a 72.6Wh battery and support fast charging with a 96W or higher USB PD power source.Connectivity options include three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, a MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip. The M5 Pro model supports up to three external displays, while the M5 Max variant can connect up to four.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 16-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 16-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The M5 Pro features an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, while the M5 Max is available with an 18-core CPU and either a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variant offers 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 16-inch MacBook Pro features a 16.3-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3472 times; 2266 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 24 hours of video streaming and 17 hours of wireless web browsing. The M5 Max variant is rated for up to 22 hours of video streaming and 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch model is lighter and more compact, and it also offers an additional M5 Pro configuration with a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU. Both models share the same core display technology, connectivity options and top-end M5 Max configurations.

story.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro

facts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.

This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

passages: SAN FRANCISCO, July 21, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Deepgram today announced an initiative to bring enterprise-grade speech recognition directly onto PCs powered by Snapdragon® processors.

By optimizing Deepgram's Nova-3 speech-to-text model on the Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU in the Snapdragon X Series platform, Deepgram is enabling developers and device manufacturers to deliver real-time voice experiences with greater speed, privacy, and reliability, without relying on a cloud connection.
This effort opens the door to further integration of voice into a new generation of intelligent applications across automotive, mobile, AI PC, XR, industrial edge, IoT, and wearable devices.
"We recognize that voice AI technologies serve different needs.

That's why we value our work with Deepgram – because accuracy, latency, reliability, and scalability matter for developers building automotive systems, healthcare applications, industrial solutions, and other mission-critical experiences," said Upendra Kulkarni, Vice President Product Management, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
Deepgram's voice-native foundation models, accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted/on-premises APIs, deliver unmatched accuracy, low latency, and competitive pricing.
Having processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed over 1 trillion words, there is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

"The future of voice-first interaction is about meeting users wherever they are — in a vehicle, on a factory floor, inside an XR headset — without compromising on accuracy or responsiveness," said Abe Pursell, Vice President, Business Development and Partnerships, Deepgram.

We're bringing Deepgram Nova-3 directly to the ecosystem of PCs with Snapdragon, providing a foundation to build voice into products that work wherever people happen to be, regardless of network conditions."
It is the first voice AI model to offer real-time multilingual transcription.
Qualcomm, Hexagon and Snapdragon are trademarks or registered trademarks of Qualcomm Incorporated.

extraction.body: Deepgram's Nova-3 speech-to-text model on PCs powered by Snapdragon ® delivers real-time voice experiences with greater speed, privacy, and reliability SAN FRANCISCO, July 21, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Deepgram today announced an initiative to bring enterprise-grade speech recognition directly onto PCs powered by Snapdragon® processors. By optimizing Deepgram's Nova-3 speech-to-text model on the Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU in the Snapdragon X Series platform, Deepgram is enabling developers and device manufacturers to deliver real-time voice experiences with greater speed, privacy, and reliability, without relying on a cloud connection. This effort opens the door to further integration of voice into a new generation of intelligent applications across automotive, mobile, AI PC, XR, industrial edge, IoT, and wearable devices. Many voice AI solutions have historically relied on a cloud-based architecture. Before a response could be delivered, each interaction required audio to leave the device, travel to the cloud, be processed somewhere else, and then return. With this approach, delays and privacy concerns are sometimes introduced, which limit where voice AI can realistically be deployed. Deepgram is fundamentally changing that model, enabling speech recognition to happen directly on the device itself. The result is an entirely new world of applications and user experiences that feel like a natural conversation, whether it is running in a vehicle, on an AI PC, inside an XR headset, or at the edge of a network where connectivity cannot be guaranteed. "We recognize that voice AI technologies serve different needs. That's why we value our work with Deepgram – because accuracy, latency, reliability, and scalability matter for developers building automotive systems, healthcare applications, industrial solutions, and other mission-critical experiences," said Upendra Kulkarni, Vice President Product Management, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. "The on-device AI capabilities of Snapdragon processors combined with Deepgram's enterprise-class voice AI uniquely bring those requirements together in a way that opens new possibilities for real-time voice experiences across the device ecosystem." "The future of voice-first interaction is about meeting users wherever they are — in a vehicle, on a factory floor, inside an XR headset — without compromising on accuracy or responsiveness," said Abe Pursell, Vice President, Business Development and Partnerships, Deepgram. "To make that possible, you need enterprise-grade speech recognition that can deliver within the constraints of a device. We're bringing Deepgram Nova-3 directly to the ecosystem of PCs with Snapdragon, providing a foundation to build voice into products that work wherever people happen to be, regardless of network conditions." Nova-3 advances Deepgram's industry-leading accuracy, extending its capabilities to a broader range of real-world enterprise use cases and challenging audio conditions. It is the first voice AI model to offer real-time multilingual transcription. Deepgram is also the first to provide users with demonstrably effective and highly accurate self-serve customization – enabling instant vocabulary adaptation without model retraining. Superior accuracy: Nova-3 leads transcription accuracy with a 6.89% word error rate on real-world production audio, a 24.7% lower error rate than the next-best competitor. Deepgram is the real-time AI infrastructure company underpinning the Voice AI economy. Today, more than 200,000 developers and 1,400 organizations are Powered by Deepgram . Its voice AI platform offers speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and full speech-to-speech (STS) capabilities, all powered by its enterprise-grade runtime. Deepgram's voice-native foundation models, accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted/on-premises APIs, deliver unmatched accuracy, low latency, and competitive pricing. Customers include technology ISVs building voice products or platforms, co-sell partners working with large enterprises, and enterprises solving internal use cases. Having processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed over 1 trillion words, there is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. To learn more, please visit www.deepgram.com , read its developer docs , or follow @DeepgramAI on X and LinkedIn . Qualcomm, Hexagon and Snapdragon are trademarks or registered trademarks of Qualcomm Incorporated.
